Q1. Marathon Multi-Segment Vector Displacement and Bearing

D2 QRT-MODEL-D2 📚 Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning 📄 2025-26 Set A 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A · Logical Reasoning · Question 1 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q001)
Official Exam Question:
During a Marathon race, Aditya runs 3 km towards East. He then turns right and runs 5 km and then turns left and runs 4 km. He again turns left and runs 8 km. Finally, he turns left and runs 2 km to reach the finishing point. How far and in which direction is he now from the starting point?
(A) 5√9 km, North-East
(B) √34 km, South-West
(C) 5√9 km, South-East
(D) √34 km, North-East
Target Mathematical Act (MODEL): Marathon Multi-Segment Vector Displacement and Bearing

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Represent each leg of Aditya's path as a Cartesian coordinate vector (dx, dy), taking East as +x and North as +y.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Compute net x = 3 + 4 - 2 = 5 km, and net y = -5 + 8 = 3 km. Use the distance formula d = √(x² + y²).

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Confused radical notation and neglected sign cancellation on vertical components.
Option B: Inverted final net displacement direction to South-West while keeping correct magnitude.
Option C: Preserved South bearing from intermediate step 2 instead of resolving final positive y-coordinate.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Sum sequential orthogonal 2D displacement vectors into net Cartesian coordinates (5, 3) and evaluate Euclidean norm

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Net horizontal = 3 + 4 - 2 = 5 km (East); Net vertical = -5 + 8 = +3 km (North). Distance √(25+9)=√34 km, direction North-East. Matches Option D uniquely.
Assign starting point at (0, 0). Vector moves: 3 km East -> (3, 0); right 5 km (South) -> (3, -5); left 4 km (East) -> (7, -5); left 8 km (North) -> (7, 3); left 2 km (West) -> (5, 3). Net displacement vector is (5, 3). Distance = √(5² + 3²) = √(25 + 9) = √34 km. Since x > 0 and y > 0, direction is North-East.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — √34 km, North-East

Q2. Parallelogram Lattice Layer Counting

D2 QRT-APPLY-D2 📚 Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning 📄 2025-26 Set A 📖 Core 1A/1B

Expected Asset: FIG-SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q002.svg
(A) 20
(B) 19
(C) 18
(D) More than 20
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Parallelogram Lattice Layer Counting

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Do not count at random. Partition the grid into single-row parallelograms and compound multi-row parallelograms.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

In a 1x3 parallelogram strip, the number of parallelograms is 3(4)/2 = 6. Evaluate row 1, row 2, and the combined 2-row lattice.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Overcounted non-existent diagonal skew combinations across non-parallel transversal boundaries.
Option B: Counted an extraneous outer bounding polygon that fails the parallel boundary definition.
Option D: Speculative guess assuming complex unseen intersections exceed 20.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Systematically count parallelograms within tier 1, tier 2, and compound vertical combinations spanning both rows

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Lattice dimension is 2 rows by 3 columns of shear parallelograms: (2 × 3 / 2) × (3 × 4 / 2) = 3 × 6 = 18. Matches Option C uniquely.
The figure consists of two rows of 3 contiguous parallelograms aligned vertically. Single row 1 contains 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 parallelograms. Single row 2 contains 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 parallelograms. Combining rows 1 and 2 vertically yields an additional 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 two-row composite parallelograms. Total count = 6 + 6 + 6 = 18.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — 18

Q3. Cubic Invariant in Radial Quadrilateral Number Puzzle

🔥 HARD OLYMPIAD CHALLENGE D3 QRT-SYNTHESIZE-D3 📚 Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning 📄 2025-26 Set A 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A · Logical Reasoning · Question 3 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q003)
🔥 Hard Olympiad · Composite Synthesis (SYNTHESIZE) Multi-step Olympiad challenge requiring intermediate formulation and invariance deduction.
Official Exam Question:
Find the missing number, if same rule is followed in all the three figures: Fig 1 has outer numbers (74, 98, 148, 112) with central 6; Fig 2 has outer numbers (32, 25, 55, 16) with central 4; Fig 3 has outer numbers (92, 35, 81, 42) with central '?'.
Figure: Official Vector Geometry (FIG-IMO-G09-2025-26-A-Q003.svg)
(A) 7
(B) 5
(C) 3
(D) 4
Target Mathematical Act (SYNTHESIZE): Cubic Invariant in Radial Quadrilateral Number Puzzle

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Find the sum of all four outer numbers in Figure 1 and Figure 2, and relate each sum to powers of the central number.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

In Fig 1, sum = 432 = 2 × 216 = 2 × 6³. In Fig 2, sum = 128 = 2 × 64 = 2 × 4³. Apply this relation to Fig 3.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed linear arithmetic difference rule without checking cubic power relationship.
Option C: Divided 250 by direct linear sum of digits instead of solving cubic invariant.
Option D: Reused central number 4 from Figure 2.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Discover the cubic summation invariant: the sum of the four outer numbers equals twice the cube of the central number

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
2 × 5³ = 2 × 125 = 250. 92 + 35 + 81 + 42 = 250. Exact match to Option B.
Calculate outer sums: Fig 1: 74 + 98 + 148 + 112 = 432. Notice 432 = 2 × 216 = 2 × 6³. Fig 2: 32 + 25 + 55 + 16 = 128. Notice 128 = 2 × 64 = 2 × 4³. For Fig 3: Sum = 92 + 35 + 81 + 42 = 250. Let center be C: 2 × C³ = 250 => C³ = 125 => C = ∛125 = 5.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — 5

Folding twice creates 4 layers. Each cutout punched in the quarter circle replicates 4 times with dual reflection symmetry.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Reflect Fig Z horizontally to unfold semi-circle Y, then vertically across the diameter to unfold full circle X.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option B: Failed horizontal mirror reflection, keeping punch in single orientation.
Option C: Rotated cutout angles by 45 degrees relative to origin.
Option D: Dropped two circle cutouts in lower hemisphere.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt

Reflect punched cutouts sequentially across vertical diameter and horizontal diameter axes

A cutout consisting of a rectangular notch on the straight boundary and two circles near the curved arc is made. Unfolding across the two perpendicular axes reflects the shapes into all 4 quadrants symmetrically, matching Option A.

Q5. Cyclic Permutation Block Letter Series

Official Exam Question:
In the given letter series, some of the letters are missing which are given in that order as one of the options below it. Select the correct option: b _ c _ a a _ c _ a b b a _ b b c c
(A) bccaa
(B) bcaab
(C) cbaca
(D) acbbc
Target Mathematical Act (REPRESENT): Cyclic Permutation Block Letter Series

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Count the total number of characters including blanks. Total length is 18. Test block partitions of length 6.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Inspect cyclic permutations of double letters: bbccaa, then ccaabb, then aabbcc.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option B: Swapped trailing letters to ab instead of aa, breaking third block symmetry.
Option C: Inverted leading character to c, disrupting initial bb pair.
Option D: Introduced singleton letters violating the double-letter invariant.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Partition 18-element series into 3 blocks of 6 letters exhibiting cyclic block shift bbccaa | ccaabb | aabbcc

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Filling 'bccaa' produces 'bbccaa | ccaabb | aabbcc'. Each block cyclically shifts the double letters by 2 positions. Matches Option A uniquely.
The series has 18 positions with 5 blanks: b [1] c [2] a a [3] c [4] a b b a [5] b b c c. Partition into 3 blocks of 6 letters: Block 1: b b c c a a (blanks at pos 2, 4 -> b, c). Block 2: c c a a b b (blanks at pos 7, 9 -> c, a). Block 3: a a b b c c (blank at pos 14 -> a). The inserted sequence is b, c, c, a, a, matching Option A.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — bccaa

Q6. Set-Theoretic Region Isolation in 4-Way Venn Diagram

D2 QRT-APPLY-D2 📚 Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning 📄 2025-26 Set A 📖 Core 1A/1B

Official Exam Question:
In the given Venn diagram, circle represents mathematicians, square represents scientists, rectangle represents men and triangle represents government employees. Which of the following letter represents women mathematicians who are scientists but not a government employee?
⚠️ VISUAL DIAGRAM CUE Set Theoretic Venn Diagram

This question relies on visual analysis of diagrammatic relationships. Visual representation cue is active.

Expected Asset: FIG-SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q006.svg
(A) p
(B) v
(C) j
(D) s
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Set-Theoretic Region Isolation in 4-Way Venn Diagram

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Women means 'not men' (outside rectangle). Not government employee means outside triangle.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Look for the region common to both Circle (mathematicians) and Square (scientists) that lies strictly outside Rectangle and Triangle.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Region p is inside the rectangle, representing men rather than women.
Option B: Region v is inside the triangle, representing government employees.
Option C: Region j is inside the rectangle, violating the women criterion.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Isolate region in Circle ∩ Square excluding Rectangle and Triangle

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Region s ∈ Circle, s ∈ Square, s ∉ Rectangle, s ∉ Triangle. Exact match to Option D.
Condition mapping: Mathematicians = Circle; Scientists = Square; Women = Outside Rectangle (not men); Not government employee = Outside Triangle. We require (Circle ∩ Square) \ (Rectangle ∪ Triangle). Inspecting the labelled regions: 'p' is inside rectangle (men); 'v' is inside triangle (gov employee); 'j' is inside rectangle; 's' lies strictly in Circle ∩ Square outside rectangle and triangle. Thus, 's' represents the required subset.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — s

Q7. 3D Dice Orthogonal Frame Reconstruction

🔥 HARD OLYMPIAD CHALLENGE D3 QRT-MODEL-D3 📚 Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning 📄 2025-26 Set A 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A · Logical Reasoning · Question 7 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q007)
🔥 Hard Olympiad · Composite Synthesis (MODEL) Multi-step Olympiad challenge requiring intermediate formulation and invariance deduction.
Official Exam Question:
Three different positions of a cube are given below. Which of the following numbers will come in place of x? Dice 1: (Top: 6, Front: 3, Right: 2); Dice 2: (Top: 1, Front: x, Right: 4); Dice 3: (Top: 5, Front: 1, Right: 2).
⚠️ VISUAL DIAGRAM CUE Orthogonal Cube Net Or Projection

This question relies on visual analysis of diagrammatic relationships. Visual representation cue is active.

Expected Asset: FIG-SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q007.svg
(A) 5
(B) 3
(C) 6
(D) 2
Target Mathematical Act (MODEL): 3D Dice Orthogonal Frame Reconstruction

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Find the numbers adjacent to face 2 in Dice 1 and Dice 3 to determine which face is opposite face 2.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

In Dice 1, adjacent to 2 are 3, 6. In Dice 3, adjacent to 2 are 1, 5. Therefore 4 is opposite 2. Then determine opposite pairs (1, 3) and (5, 6).

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option B: Face 3 is opposite to Top face 1, so it cannot be adjacent on the Front face.
Option C: Face 6 is opposite to Front face 5, representing the Back face.
Option D: Face 2 is opposite to Right face 4, representing the Left face.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Deduce opposite face pairings from shared face 2, then orient face axes to solve missing front face x in Dice 2

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Right-hand rule: Top=1 (+z), Right=4 (+x). With 1 opposite 3 and 4 opposite 2, the front (+y) must be face 5. Matches Option A uniquely.
From Dice 1 and 3, face 2 is adjacent to 3, 6, 1, 5. Hence face 4 must be opposite face 2. Between Dice 1 and Dice 3: rotating around face 2 from (Top 6, Front 3) to (Top 5, Front 1) reveals that 6 is opposite 5, and 3 is opposite 1. For Dice 2: Top is 1, Right is 4. Since 4 is opposite 2, looking at the cube with 4 on Right and 1 on Top places face 5 directly in Front. Therefore x = 5.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — 5

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Found only adjacent pair (S, T) and missed non-adjacent pairs.

✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt

(Forward pair). 2) (T, R): in word, 1 letter (E) between; in alphabet, |20 - 18| - 1 = 1. (Backward pair: R, S, T). 3) (M, R): in word, 4 letters (A, S, T, E) between; in alphabet, |18 - 13| - 1 = 4 (N, O, P, Q). (Forward pair: M to R). No other pairs satisfy the condition. Total pairs = 3.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — Three

Q11. Circular Radial Outward Seating Permutation

🔥 HARD OLYMPIAD CHALLENGE D3 QRT-SYNTHESIZE-D3 📚 Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning 📄 2025-26 Set A 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A · Logical Reasoning · Question 11 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q011)
🔥 Hard Olympiad · Composite Synthesis (SYNTHESIZE) Multi-step Olympiad challenge requiring intermediate formulation and invariance deduction.
Official Exam Question:
Seven teachers K, L, M, N, O, P and Q are sitting in a circle facing opposite to the centre of the circle. P is third to the left of L. K is fourth to the left of O. N is second to the right of P and M is sitting exactly between O and L. What is the position of Q with respect to K?
(A) Third to the left
(B) Second to the left
(C) Fourth to the right
(D) Third to the right
Target Mathematical Act (SYNTHESIZE): Circular Radial Outward Seating Permutation

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Remember: when persons face outward (opposite to centre), 'left' corresponds to clockwise motion and 'right' corresponds to anti-clockwise motion.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Fix L at position 0. P is 3rd to left (clockwise) -> position 3. N is 2nd to right of P (anti-clockwise) -> position 1. Place M between O and L.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed inward-facing convention where clockwise corresponds to right.
Option C: Counted anti-clockwise from K to Q without reversing for outward facing.
Option D: Misplaced M at position 1 instead of N.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Construct 7-person circular outward arrangement where left/right directions are inverted relative to standard center-facing tables

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
From K(2), moving clockwise (facing outwards = left): pos 3 (P), pos 4 (Q). Exactly 2nd to the left. Matches Option B uniquely.
Number 7 circular positions clockwise 0 to 6. Facing outward: Left = Clockwise (+), Right = Anti-clockwise (-). 1) Fix L at pos 0. P is 3rd to left of L -> pos 3. 2) N is 2nd to right of P -> pos 3 - 2 = pos 1. 3) M is between O and L: since L is at 0, M must be at 6 and O at 5 (since pos 1 is occupied by N). 4) K is 4th to left of O -> pos (5 + 4) mod 7 = pos 2. 5) Remaining seat for Q is pos 4. Positions clockwise: L(0), N(1), K(2), P(3), Q(4), O(5), M(6). Position of Q(4) with respect to K(2): moving clockwise (left) from K to Q is (4 - 2) = 2 steps. Hence Q is second to the left of K.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — Second to the left

Q14. Coded Operator Generation Hierarchy in Extended Pedigree

D2 QRT-JUSTIFY-D2 📚 Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning 📄 2025-26 Set A 📖 Core 1A/1B

Which of the following is definitely true for the expression A - R + N ÷ P × L?
(A) L is the grandfather of R.
(B) P is the father of R.
(C) N is the daughter of L.
(D) A is the son of L.
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Coded Operator Generation Hierarchy in Extended Pedigree

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: The gender of L is unspecified; L could be grandmother or grandfather of R.

⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Decode syntactic operator chain A - R + N ÷ P × L to establish paternity and generational descent

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
A is male; P is A's wife; P is daughter-in-law of L => A is L's son. Gender of L is unknown, so A (grandfather) cannot be asserted. Option D is definitely true.
1) A - R: A is the father of R (A is male). 2) R + N: R is brother of N. 3) N ÷ P: N is daughter of P. Since A is father of R and N, and N is daughter of P, P is the mother of R and N, meaning A and P are husband and wife. 4) P × L: P is the daughter-in-law of L. Since P is married to A, P being the daughter-in-law of L implies that A is the son of L. Therefore, 'A is the son of L' is definitely true.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — A is the son of L.

Q16. Symmetric Rational Sum Under Zero Sum Constraint

Official Exam Question:
If p + q + r = 0, then the value of (q + r)²/(qr) + (p + r)²/(pr) + (p + q)²/(pq) is:
(A) 1
(B) 3
(C) 2
(D) 0
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Symmetric Rational Sum Under Zero Sum Constraint

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Since p + q + r = 0, substitute q + r = -p, p + r = -q, and p + q = -r into the numerators.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

The expression simplifies to p²/(qr) + q²/(pr) + r²/(pq) = (p³ + q³ + r³)/(pqr). What is p³ + q³ + r³ when p + q + r = 0?

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed terms cancel to 1.
Option C: Dropped the third term or miscalculated numerator exponent.
Option D: Conflated the value of the sum with the zero condition p + q + r = 0.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Apply q+r = -p to rewrite numerators as p², q², r², then invoke the conditional identity p³+q³+r³ = 3pqr

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Let p = 1, q = 1, r = -2 (sum = 0). (q+r)²/(qr) = (-1)²/(-2) = -1/2. (p+r)²/(pr) = (-1)²/(-2) = -1/2. (p+q)²/(pq) = (2)²/(1) = 4. Sum = -1/2 - 1/2 + 4 = 3. Invariant holds.
Given p + q + r = 0, we have q + r = -p => (q + r)² = (-p)² = p². Similarly, (p + r)² = q² and (p + q)² = r². The expression becomes: p²/(qr) + q²/(pr) + r²/(pq) = (p³ + q³ + r³)/(pqr). From the fundamental identity, if p + q + r = 0, then p³ + q³ + r³ = 3pqr. Therefore, the expression equals 3pqr / pqr = 3.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — 3

(B) 138.16 cm²
(C) 34.54 cm²
(D) 766.16 cm²
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Dual Sphere Radii Reconstruction and Surface Area Differential

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Sphere volume is proportional to the cube of the radius: V₁/V₂ = (r₁/r₂)³. Take the cube root of 216/125.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

r₁/r₂ = 6/5. Since r₁ + r₂ = 11, find r₁ and r₂. Then compute ΔA = 4π(r₁² - r₂²).

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Transposed digits 138.16 to 183.16.
Option C: Computed linear radius difference times π: 3.14 × 11 = 34.54.
Option D: Added the surface areas instead of subtracting.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Extract radius ratio r₁/r₂ = ∛(216/125) = 6/5, solve system with r₁+r₂=11, and evaluate 4π(r₁² - r₂²)

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
4 × 3.14 × 11 = 138.16 cm². V₁/V₂ = 6³/5³ = 216/125. Exact match to Option B.
Volume ratio V₁/V₂ = r₁³/r₂³ = 216/125 => r₁/r₂ = ∛216 / ∛125 = 6/5. Let r₁ = 6k, r₂ = 5k. Sum of radii: 6k + 5k = 11k = 11 cm => k = 1. Thus r₁ = 6 cm and r₂ = 5 cm. Total surface area difference: ΔA = 4πr₁² - 4πr₂² = 4π(6² - 5²) = 4π(36 - 25) = 4π(11) = 44π cm². Using π = 3.14: ΔA = 44 × 3.14 = 138.16 cm².
Verified Answer: Option (B) — 138.16 cm²

Expand (y + 1/y)(y + 1/y - 2) = (y + 1/y)² - 2(y + 1/y) = y² + 2 + 1/y² - 2y - 2/y. Exact match to the given polynomial.
Rewrite the expression by grouping terms: (y² + 1/y² + 2) - (2y + 2/y). The first group is (y + 1/y)². The second group is -2(y + 1/y). Thus: (y + 1/y)² - 2(y + 1/y) = (y + 1/y)(y + 1/y - 2). The factors are (y + 1/y) and (y + 1/y - 2). Among the given options, (y + 1/y - 2) is Option B.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — y + 1/y - 2

Identify canonical Euclidean axioms (whole > part, doubles of equals are equal, halves of equals are equal) and spot fraudulent option D

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
If a = b, a + b = 2a ≠ (1/3)a. Option D is false and therefore not an axiom.
Euclid's common notions include: Axiom 1: Things equal to the same thing are equal to one another. Axiom 2: If equals are added to equals, the wholes are equal. Axiom 3: If equals are subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal. Axiom 4: Things which coincide with one another are equal to one another. Axiom 5: The whole is greater than the part (Option A). Axiom 6: Things which are double of the same things are equal (Option B). Axiom 7: Things which are halves of the same things are equal (Option C). Option D states an arbitrary false relation ('their sum is equal to 1/3 of the one thing', whereas if two things are equal, their sum is double, not 1/3). Therefore, D is not an axiom.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — If two things are equal, then their sum is equal to 1/3 of the one thing.

(B) ₹ 3600
(C) ₹ 4800
(D) ₹ 2400

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

A: 16000×3 + 11000×9 = 147000. B: 12000×3 + 17000×9 = 189000. C: 21000×6 = 126000. Ratio = 147 : 189 : 126 = 7 : 9 : 6. Find (9 - 6)/22 × 17600.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert

B's profit = 9 × 800 = ₹ 7200. C's profit = 6 × 800 = ₹ 4800. B - C = 7200 - 4800 = ₹ 2400. Matches Option D uniquely.
1) Calculate equivalent month-capitals over 12 months: A: 16000 × 3 + (16000 - 5000) × 9 = 48000 + 11000 × 9 = 48000 + 99000 = ₹ 147,000. B: 12000 × 3 + (12000 + 5000) × 9 = 36000 + 17000 × 9 = 36000 + 153000 = ₹ 189,000. C joins after 3 + 3 = 6 months, active for remaining 6 months: 21000 × 6 = ₹ 126,000. 2) Ratio of profits A : B : C = 147000 : 189000 : 126000 = 147 : 189 : 126. Divide by 21: 147/21 = 7, 189/21 = 9, 126/21 = 6. Ratio A : B : C = 7 : 9 : 6. 3) Total ratio parts = 7 + 9 + 6 = 22. Value of 1 part = 17600 / 22 = ₹ 800. 4) Excess of B's share over C's share = (9 - 6) parts = 3 parts = 3 × ₹ 800 = ₹ 2,400.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — ₹ 2400

Evaluate Statement (i): 1/x = 2 - √3 => x = 1/(2 - √3) = 2 + √3. Then x - 2 = √3. Squaring both sides: (x - 2)² = 3 => x² - 4x + 4 = 3 => x² - 4x + 1 = 0. Rewrite polynomial: x³ - 2x² - 7x + 5 = x(x² - 4x + 1) + 2x² - 8x + 5 = x(0) + 2(x² - 4x + 1) + 3 = 0 + 0 + 3 = 3. Since the statement claims the value is 5, Statement (i) is FALSE. Evaluate Statement (ii): 'Square root of a positive real number is always an irrational number.' Counterexample: 4 is a positive real number, and √4 = 2, which is rational. 9 is a positive real number, and √9 = 3, which is rational. Hence, Statement (ii) is FALSE. Evaluate Statement (iii): a = √(6 - √11), b = √(6 + √11). Compute (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab = (6 - √11) + (6 + √11) + 2√[(6 - √11)(6 + √11)] = 12 + 2√(36 - 11) = 12 + 2√25 = 12 + 2(5) = 12 + 10 = 22. Therefore, a + b = √22. The statement claims a + b = √23, which is FALSE. Thus, all three statements are False: (i) F, (ii) F, (iii) F, corresponding to Option A.

Statement-I: Half-chords are 3 cm and 4 cm. r² = 3² + 4² = 25 => r = 5. Distance d = √(5² - 4²) = 3 cm (True). Statement-II: ABFE is cyclic => ∠BFE = 180° - ∠A. ABCD is cyclic => ∠C = 180° - ∠A. Since ∠BFE = ∠C, EF || DC (True).

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Statement-I: d = √(5² - 4²) = 3 cm (Exact). Statement-II: ∠EFB = ∠C = 180° - ∠A => EF || DC by corresponding angles converse theorem. Both statements are rigorously proved true. Option A is exact.
Proof of Statement-I: Let the circle have radius r. The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord. For the chord of length 6 cm: half-length = 3 cm, distance from centre = 4 cm. By Pythagorean theorem: r² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 => r = 5 cm. For the other parallel chord of length 8 cm: half-length = 4 cm. Its distance d from the centre satisfies: d² + 4² = r² = 25 => d² = 25 - 16 = 9 => d = 3 cm. Thus, Statement-I is TRUE. Proof of Statement-II: Quadrilateral ABFE is cyclic (vertices A, B, F, E all lie on the inner circle). In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is 180°: ∠A + ∠EFB = 180° => ∠EFB = 180° - ∠A. Quadrilateral ABCD is also cyclic (vertices A, B, C, D lie on the outer circle). Hence: ∠A + ∠C = 180° => ∠C = 180° - ∠A. Comparing the two equations: ∠EFB = ∠C. But ∠EFB and ∠C are corresponding angles for lines EF and DC intersected by transversal line BC. Since the corresponding angles are equal, line EF must be parallel to line DC (EF || DC). Thus, Statement-II is TRUE. Therefore, Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true, corresponding to Option A.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.

Q66. Difference of Conjugate Radicals and Coefficient Identification

(B) 3/2
(C) -2/3
(D) -(3\sqrt{7})/2
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Difference of Conjugate Radicals and Coefficient Identification

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Combine the two fractions over the common denominator $(\sqrt{7}+1)(\sqrt{7}-1) = 7 - 1 = 6$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Numerator is $(\sqrt{7}-1)^2 - (\sqrt{7}+1)^2 = -4\sqrt{7}$. Simplify the fraction and match with $p - q\sqrt{7}$.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option B: Inverted numerator and denominator ($3/2$).
Option C: Sign error forgetting the negative sign in $-q\sqrt{7}$, setting $q = -2/3$.
Option D: Carried radical factor into denominator.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Subtract conjugate fractions by taking LCM $(a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2$ and equate radical coefficient to $-q$

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Rationalize separately: $(4-\sqrt{7})/3 - (4+\sqrt{7})/3 = -2\sqrt{7}/3$. Since $-q\sqrt{7} = -2/3\sqrt{7}$, $q = 2/3$. Exact.
LHS $= \frac{(\sqrt{7}-1)^2 - (\sqrt{7}+1)^2}{(\sqrt{7}+1)(\sqrt{7}-1)} = \frac{(8 - 2\sqrt{7}) - (8 + 2\sqrt{7})}{7 - 1} = \frac{-4\sqrt{7}}{6} = -\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{7}$. Equating to $p - q\sqrt{7}$, we get $p = 0$ and $-q = -2/3 \implies q = 2/3$.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — 2/3

Q68. Exponential Equation Base-2 Reduction and Target Evaluation

D2 QRT-APPLY-D2 📚 Number Systems 📄 2025-26 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Mathematical Reasoning · Question 18 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q018)
Official Exam Question:
If $\frac{4^{n+3} \times 8^{3-n}}{(64^{-n/2})} = 2^9 \times 4^{3n}$, then find the value of $2n$.
(A) 3/2
(B) 2
(C) 3
(D) 2/3
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Exponential Equation Base-2 Reduction and Target Evaluation

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Rewrite every base as a power of 2: $4 = 2^2$, $8 = 2^3$, $64 = 2^6$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

LHS numerator: $2^{2n+6 + 9-3n} = 2^{15-n}$. Denominator: $(2^6)^{-n/2} = 2^{-3n}$. LHS $= 2^{15+2n}$. Equate to RHS $= 2^{9+6n}$.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Reported the value of $n = 3/2$ instead of requested target $2n$.
Option B: Arithmetic slip setting $4n = 8 \implies n = 1, 2n = 2$.
Option D: Inverted fraction $2/3$.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Express all terms as powers of base 2: $4=2^2, 8=2^3, 64=2^6$, solve for $n$, then compute target $2n$

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Substitute $n = 1.5$: LHS $= 4^{4.5} \times 8^{1.5} / 64^{-0.75} = 512 \times 22.627 / 0.04419 = 262144 = 2^{18}$. RHS $= 512 \times 4^{4.5} = 512 \times 512 = 262144$. Match confirmed. $2n = 3$.
Convert to base 2:
LHS Numerator $= 2^{2(n+3)} \times 2^{3(3-n)} = 2^{2n+6 + 9-3n} = 2^{15-n}$
LHS Denominator $= (2^6)^{-n/2} = 2^{-3n}$
LHS $= 2^{(15-n) - (-3n)} = 2^{2n+15}$
RHS $= 2^9 \times (2^2)^{3n} = 2^{9+6n}$
Equating exponents: $2n + 15 = 6n + 9 \implies 4n = 6 \implies n = 3/2$.
Target is $2n = 2(3/2) = 3$.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — 3

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

$\angle OBA = \angle OAB = 50^\circ$, and $\angle OBC = \angle OCB = 35^\circ$. Thus $\angle B = 50^\circ + 35^\circ = 85^\circ$. What is the relationship between $\angle B$ and $\angle D$ in cyclic quad $ABCD$?

Compute $\angle ABC$ from isosceles $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle OBC$, then use cyclic property $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - \angle ABC$

✓ Formal Verification (ALTERNATE_METHOD)
Reflex central angle $\angle AOC = 2 \times \angle ADC = 2 \times 95^\circ = 190^\circ$. Minor $\angle AOC = 360^\circ - 190^\circ = 170^\circ$. In $\triangle OAC$, angles at $O$ from $\triangle OAB$ ($80^\circ$) and $\triangle OBC$ ($110^\circ$) sum to $80+110=190$ reflex. Exact agreement.
In $\triangle OAB$, $OA = OB$ (radii) $\implies \angle OBA = \angle OAB = 50^\circ$.
In $\triangle OBC$, $OB = OC$ (radii) $\implies \angle OBC = \angle OCB = 35^\circ$.
Total $\angle B = \angle OBA + \angle OBC = 50^\circ + 35^\circ = 85^\circ$.
Since points $A, B, C, D$ lie on the circle, $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.
Opposite angles sum to $180^\circ$: $\angle ADC = x = 180^\circ - \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 85^\circ = 95^\circ$.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — 95°

Vertically opposite angles: $\angle XON = \angle MOY = \angle MOP + \angle POY = a + 90^\circ = 36^\circ + 90^\circ = 126^\circ$. Matches identically.
Line $XY$ is straight and $OP \perp XY \implies \angle POX = 90^\circ$. Since $\angle POX = a + b = 90^\circ$ and $a:b = 2:3$, let $a = 2k, b = 3k \implies 5k = 90^\circ \implies k = 18^\circ$. Thus $b = 3(18^\circ) = 54^\circ$ and $a = 36^\circ$. Since line $MN$ is a straight line, $\angle MOX + \angle XON = 180^\circ \implies b + \angle XON = 180^\circ \implies \angle XON = 180^\circ - 54^\circ = 126^\circ$.

Q75. Quartic Polynomial Factor Theorem Parity Invariant

🔥 HARD OLYMPIAD CHALLENGE D3 QRT-JUSTIFY-D3 📚 Polynomials 📄 2025-26 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Mathematical Reasoning · Question 25 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q025)
🔥 Hard Olympiad · Composite Synthesis (JUSTIFY) Multi-step Olympiad challenge requiring intermediate formulation and invariance deduction.
Official Exam Question:
If $x^2 - 1$ is a factor of $ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + dx + e$, then select the correct option.
(A) a + b + e = c + d
(B) a + b + c = d + e
(C) b + c + d = a + e
(D) None of these
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Quartic Polynomial Factor Theorem Parity Invariant

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Factor $x^2 - 1$ as $(x-1)(x+1)$. By the factor theorem, both $P(1) = 0$ and $P(-1) = 0$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

$P(1) = a + b + c + d + e = 0$ and $P(-1) = a - b + c - d + e = 0$. Add and subtract these two equations.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Falsely combined even and odd power coefficients.
Option B: Mixed leading coefficients with trailing linear/constant terms.
Option C: Transposed terms arbitrarily.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Decompose $x^2-1 = (x-1)(x+1) \implies P(1)=0$ and $P(-1)=0$; deduce $a+c+e=0$ and $b+d=0$, ruling out options A, B, C

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Counterexample for A, B, C: Let $P(x) = (x^2-1)(x^2-4) = x^4 - 5x^2 + 4$. Here $a=1, b=0, c=-5, d=0, e=4$. $a+c+e = 1-5+4 = 0$ and $b+d = 0$. Test A: $1+0+4=5 \ne -5+0$. Test B: $1+0-5=-4 \ne 0+4$. Test C: $0-5+0=-5 \ne 1+4$. All false. D holds.
Since $x^2 - 1 = (x-1)(x+1)$ is a factor of $P(x)$:
$P(1) = a + b + c + d + e = 0 \implies (a+c+e) + (b+d) = 0$
$P(-1) = a - b + c - d + e = 0 \implies (a+c+e) - (b+d) = 0$
Adding gives $2(a+c+e) = 0 \implies a + c + e = 0$.
Subtracting gives $2(b+d) = 0 \implies b + d = 0$.
Hence $a + c + e = b + d = 0$. None of the relations in A, B, or C ($a+b+e = c+d$, etc.) generally holds. Therefore, Option D is correct.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — None of these

Option C: Added 1 instead of subtracting 1 ($1 + 1 = 2$).
Option D: Assumed product evaluates to 0, getting $0 - 1 = -1$.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Apply exponent identity $(a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2) = a^3 - b^3$; cyclic sum telescoping yields $x^0 - 1 = 1 - 1 = 0$

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Substitute $a=1, b=2, c=3, x=2$: Product evaluates to $2^{(1-8)+(8-27)+(27-1)} = 2^0 = 1$. $1 - 1 = 0$. Confirmed.
Using quotient rule and identity $(u-v)(u^2+uv+v^2) = u^3 - v^3$:
First term $= (x^{a-b})^{a^2+ab+b^2} = x^{a^3 - b^3}$
Second term $= x^{b^3 - c^3}$
Third term $= x^{c^3 - a^3}$
Product $= x^{(a^3-b^3) + (b^3-c^3) + (c^3-a^3)} = x^0 = 1$.
Full expression $= 1 - 1 = 0$.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — 0

Q77. Coordinate Axes Intercepts and Hypotenuse Segment Length

Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

$5x = 60 \implies x = 12$ so $P = (12, 0)$. $12y = 60 \implies y = 5$ so $Q = (0, 5)$. Use distance formula $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}$.

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Pythagorean triple $(5, 12, 13)$. Since $OP = 12$ and $OQ = 5$ with $OP \perp OQ$, $PQ^2 = 12^2 + 5^2 = 169 \implies PQ = 13$.
Intercepts:
At $y = 0$: $5x = 60 \implies x = 12 \implies P = (12, 0)$.
At $x = 0$: $12y = 60 \implies y = 5 \implies Q = (0, 5)$.
Length $PQ = \sqrt{(12 - 0)^2 + (0 - 5)^2} = \sqrt{144 + 25} = \sqrt{169} = 13$ units.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — 13 units

Q78. Wood Carving Waste Percentage from Cuboid to Cone

A cone of height $14\text{ cm}$ and base radius $1\text{ cm}$ is carved from a cuboidal block of wood $15\text{ cm} \times 5\text{ cm} \times 2\text{ cm}$. Assuming $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, what is the percentage of wood wasted in the process?

(B) 92 2/3 %
(C) 53 2/3 %
(D) None of these

Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

$V_{\text{cuboid}} = 150\text{ cm}^3$. $V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 1^2 \times 14 = \frac{44}{3}\text{ cm}^3$. Wasted volume $= 150 - \frac{44}{3} = \frac{406}{3}\text{ cm}^3$. Compute percentage.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option B: Approximated $\pi = 3.14$ or rounded $44/3$ incorrectly to $14$.

Option D: Calculation error in fraction simplification.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Compute cuboid volume 150, cone volume 44/3, waste volume 406/3, and percentage $\frac{406/3}{150} \times 100 = 90\frac{2}{9}\%$

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
$90 \times 9 + 2 = 812$. $812 / 9 \times 1.5 = 812 / 6 = 135.333\text{ cm}^3$. $135.333 + 14.667 = 150\text{ cm}^3$. Exact.
$V_{\text{cuboid}} = 15 \times 5 \times 2 = 150\text{ cm}^3$.
$V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 1^2 \times 14 = \frac{44}{3}\text{ cm}^3$.
$V_{\text{wasted}} = 150 - \frac{44}{3} = \frac{450 - 44}{3} = \frac{406}{3}\text{ cm}^3$.
Percentage wasted $= \frac{406/3}{150} \times 100\% = \frac{40600}{450}\% = \frac{812}{9}\% = 90\frac{2}{9}\%$.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — 90 2/9 %

Q80. Rational Algebraic Identity and Factor Verification

Official Exam Question:

(A) The greatest common factor of $x^2 y^3$ and $x^3 y^2$ is $x^2 y^2$.
(B) $x - 3y$ is a factor of $x^4 - 9x^2 y^2$.
(C) $\frac{3x^5 - 3x}{3x^3 + 3x} = x^2 + 1$
(D) $2x - 1$ is a factor of $4x^2 - 1$.
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Rational Algebraic Identity and Factor Verification

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Factorize the numerator and denominator of the expression in Option C: $3x^5 - 3x = 3x(x^4 - 1)$ and $3x^3 + 3x = 3x(x^2 + 1)$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

$\frac{3x(x^2-1)(x^2+1)}{3x(x^2+1)} = x^2 - 1$. Does this equal $x^2 + 1$?

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: True mathematical property of monomial GCD.
Option B: True factorization of difference of squares.
Option D: True standard binomial factorization.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Factorize numerator and denominator in Option C: $\frac{3x(x^4-1)}{3x(x^2+1)} = x^2 - 1 \ne x^2 + 1$

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Substitute $x = 2$: LHS $= (3(32)-6)/(3(8)+6) = 90 / 30 = 3$. RHS of C $= 2^2 + 1 = 5$. Since $3 \ne 5$, C is false.
Analyzing statement C:
$\frac{3x^5 - 3x}{3x^3 + 3x} = \frac{3x(x^4 - 1)}{3x(x^2 + 1)} = \frac{3x(x^2 - 1)(x^2 + 1)}{3x(x^2 + 1)} = x^2 - 1$.
The claim states it equals $x^2 + 1$, which is false for all real $x$ (since $x^2 - 1 \ne x^2 + 1$). Thus C is NOT correct.
A is correct: $\gcd(x^2y^3, x^3y^2) = x^{\min(2,3)} y^{\min(3,2)} = x^2 y^2$.
B is correct: $x^4 - 9x^2y^2 = x^2(x^2-9y^2) = x^2(x-3y)(x+3y)$, so $x-3y$ is a factor.
D is correct: $4x^2 - 1 = (2x-1)(2x+1)$, so $2x-1$ is a factor.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — (3x^5 - 3x)/(3x^3 + 3x) = x^2 + 1

⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
In $\Delta FDE$, angles are $\angle F=80^\circ, \angle D=40^\circ, \angle E=60^\circ$. Sum $= 180^\circ$. Side $DF = 5\text{ cm}$. Confirms Option B.
Given $\Delta ABC \cong \Delta FDE$:
Corresponding sides: $AB = FD = 5\text{ cm}$, $BC = DE$, $AC = FE$.
Corresponding angles: $\angle A = \angle F = 80^\circ$, $\angle B = \angle D = 40^\circ$, $\angle C = \angle E$.
In $\Delta ABC$, $\angle C = 180^\circ - (\angle A + \angle B) = 180^\circ - (80^\circ + 40^\circ) = 60^\circ$.
Therefore $\angle E = 60^\circ$ and $DF = 5\text{ cm}$. Matches Option B.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — DF = 5 cm, ∠E = 60°

(B) 22 cm
(C) 28 cm
(D) 11 cm

The length of the midline connecting the midpoints of the non-parallel sides of a trapezium is the average of the two parallel bases: $PQ = \frac{AB + CD}{2}$.

✓ Formal Verification (ALTERNATE_METHOD)
Standard midline theorem: $PQ = (AB + CD)/2 = (14 + 8)/2 = 22/2 = 11\text{ cm}$. Identical result.
Draw diagonal $BD$ meeting $PQ$ at $M$.
In $\triangle ABD$, $P$ is midpoint of $AD$ and $PM \parallel AB$. By converse of mid-point theorem, $M$ is midpoint of $BD$ and $PM = \frac{1}{2} AB = \frac{1}{2}(14) = 7\text{ cm}$.
In $\triangle BCD$, $M$ is midpoint of $BD$ and $MQ \parallel CD$. Thus $Q$ is midpoint of $BC$ and $MQ = \frac{1}{2} CD = \frac{1}{2}(8) = 4\text{ cm}$.
Total length $PQ = PM + MQ = 7 + 4 = 11\text{ cm}$.

Q85. Non-Associativity of Subtraction over Rational Field

D1 QRT-EXPLAIN-D1 📚 Number Systems 📄 2025-26 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Mathematical Reasoning · Question 35 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q035)

Which of the following statements is incorrect?
(A) If $a$ and $b$ are consecutive rational numbers where $a < b$, then $a < \frac{a+b}{2} < b$.
(B) $\frac{x+y}{2}$ is a rational number which lies between $x$ and $y$.
(C) Rational numbers are associative under subtraction.
(D) The rational numbers $\frac{5}{3}$ and $\frac{-1}{3}$ are lying on the opposite sides of '0' on the number line.
Target Mathematical Act (EXPLAIN): Non-Associativity of Subtraction over Rational Field

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Test the associative property with concrete numbers: does $(a - b) - c = a - (b - c)$?

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Let $a = 1, b = 2, c = 3$. $(1 - 2) - 3 = -1 - 3 = -4$. But $1 - (2 - 3) = 1 - (-1) = 2$. Since $-4 \ne 2$, subtraction is NOT associative.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: True density property of rational numbers.
Option B: True mean theorem for real/rational numbers.
Option D: True statement: positive rationals lie to the right of 0, negative to the left.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Identify that subtraction is non-associative: $(a-b)-c \ne a-(b-c)$, making C incorrect

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
$(5 - 3) - 2 = 0$, but $5 - (3 - 2) = 4$. $0 \ne 4$. Disproves associativity.
The associative property of an operation requires $(a * b) * c = a * (b * c)$. For subtraction:
$(a - b) - c = a - b - c$
$a - (b - c) = a - b + c$
These expressions differ by $2c$, which is nonzero whenever $c \ne 0$. Hence subtraction is NOT associative over the rational numbers, making statement C incorrect.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — Rational numbers are associative under subtraction.

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Stop locations: 90, 180, 270, 360, 450, 540, 630 km (7 stops). At 720 km the journey concludes. $7 \times 3 = 21$ mins. Total = 6 hrs 21 mins.
Pure motion time $= \frac{720\text{ km}}{120\text{ km/h}} = 6\text{ hours}$.
The train stops after every $90\text{ km}$. Number of intermediate intervals $= \frac{720}{90} = 8$.
The 8th stop occurs at the arrival destination; thus there are $8 - 1 = 7$ en-route stops.
Total stoppage time $= 7 \times 3\text{ minutes} = 21\text{ minutes}$.
Total journey time $= 6\text{ hours } 21\text{ minutes}$.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — 6 hrs 21 mins

Coin radius $r = 0.7 = \frac{7}{10}\text{ cm}$, thickness $h = 0.4 = \frac{4}{10}\text{ cm}$. Number of coins $N = \frac{\pi R^2 H}{\pi r^2 h} = \frac{R^2 H}{r^2 h}$.

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
$250 \times V_C = 250 \times \frac{49\pi}{250} = 49\pi = V_B$. Exact integer match: 250.
Base dimensions: $R = 3.5 / 2 = 1.75\text{ cm} = 7/4\text{ cm}$, $H = 16\text{ cm}$.
Base Volume $V_B = \pi R^2 H = \pi \left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 (16) = \pi \left(\frac{49}{16}\right) (16) = 49\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Coin dimensions: $r = 1.4 / 2 = 0.7\text{ cm} = 7/10\text{ cm}$, $h = 0.4\text{ cm} = 4/10\text{ cm}$.
Coin Volume $V_C = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{7}{10}\right)^2 \left(\frac{4}{10}\right) = \pi \left(\frac{49}{100}\right) \left(\frac{4}{10}\right) = \frac{196\pi}{1000} = \frac{49\pi}{250}\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of coins $N = \frac{V_B}{V_C} = \frac{49\pi}{\frac{49\pi}{250}} = 250$.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — 250

Q93. Quadratic Area Scaling in Similar Geometric Concentric Regions

(A) 4 : 3
(B) 5 : 4
(C) 1 : 3
(D) 2 : 3
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Quadratic Area Scaling in Similar Geometric Concentric Regions

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

The ratio of areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Side ratio $s_{\text{park}} / s_{\text{bed}} = 1.5 = 3/2$. Total area ratio $A_{\text{park}} / A_{\text{bed}} = (3/2)^2 = 9/4$. Path area $= A_{\text{park}} - A_{\text{bed}}$.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Took ratio of flower bed to path inverted ($4 : 5$ or $4 : 3$).
Option C: Used linear scaling factor ($1.5 - 1 = 0.5 \implies 1 : 2$).
Option D: Inverted side ratio ($2 : 3$).
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Area ratio is square of linear ratio $(1.5)^2 = 9/4$; path area is $9 - 4 = 5$, giving ratio $5 : 4$

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Let flower bed have base 4, height 2 -> Area = 4. Park has base 6, height 3 -> Area = 9. Path = 9 - 4 = 5. Ratio path : bed = 5 : 4. Exact.
Since the park and the flower bed are similar triangles:
Linear scaling ratio $k = \frac{\text{side}_{\text{park}}}{\text{side}_{\text{bed}}} = 1.5 = \frac{3}{2}$.
Ratio of total park area to flower bed area is $k^2 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}$.
Let $A_{\text{bed}} = 4$ units. Then $A_{\text{park}} = 9$ units.
The path area $= A_{\text{park}} - A_{\text{bed}} = 9 - 4 = 5$ units.
Ratio of path area to flower bed area $= \frac{A_{\text{path}}}{A_{\text{bed}}} = \frac{5}{4} = 5 : 4$.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — 5 : 4

Q94. Combined Inflow Work Rates with Bottom Leakage Delay

🔥 HARD OLYMPIAD CHALLENGE D3 QRT-MODEL-D3 📚 Quantitative Aptitude 📄 2025-26 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Everyday Mathematics · Question 44 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q044)
🔥 Hard Olympiad · Composite Synthesis (MODEL) Multi-step Olympiad challenge requiring intermediate formulation and invariance deduction.
Official Exam Question:
Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to leakage in the bottom, it took 80 minutes more to fill the cistern. When the cistern is full, in what time will the leak empty it?
(A) 17 hours
(B) 18 hours
(C) 19 hours
(D) None of these
Target Mathematical Act (MODEL): Combined Inflow Work Rates with Bottom Leakage Delay

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Find the combined filling rate of pipes A and B without the leak: $\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15}$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Normal fill time $= \frac{60}{9} = \frac{20}{3}\text{ hours} = 6\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$. Adding 80 minutes delay gives 8 hours. The leak rate is $(A+B) - \text{Net Rate} = \frac{3}{20} - \frac{1}{8}$.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Selected 17 hours by flawed linear subtraction.
Option B: Selected 18 hours by forgetting common denominator factor.
Option C: Selected 19 hours from approximation.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Combined fill rate $1/12 + 1/15 = 3/20$ (time 6h 40m); with 80m leak delay time is 8h (rate 1/8); leak rate $3/20 - 1/8 = 1/40 \implies 40\text{ hrs}$, hence 'None of these'

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Net rate $= 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/40 = 10/120 + 8/120 - 3/120 = 15/120 = 1/8$ cistern/hr. Fill time $= 8\text{ hrs}$. Delay $= 8\text{ hrs} - 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} = 80\text{ mins}$. Confirms 40 hours uniquely.
Fill rate of pipe A $= 1/12$ cistern/hr.
Fill rate of pipe B $= 1/15$ cistern/hr.
Combined rate $(A + B) = \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{5 + 4}{60} = \frac{9}{60} = \frac{3}{20}\text{ cistern/hr}$.
Normal time to fill cistern $= \frac{20}{3}\text{ hours} = 6\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$.
Due to the leak, time taken $= 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} + 80\text{ mins} = 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} + 1\text{ hr } 20\text{ mins} = 8\text{ hours}$.
Net filling rate with leak $= \frac{1}{8}\text{ cistern/hr}$.
Let the emptying rate of the leak be $L$.
$\frac{3}{20} - L = \frac{1}{8} \implies L = \frac{3}{20} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{6 - 5}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\text{ cistern/hr}$.
Thus, the leak alone empties the full cistern in $\frac{1}{1/40} = 40\text{ hours}$.
Since $40\text{ hours}$ is not 17, 18, or 19 hours, the correct option is 'None of these'.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — None of these

(C) ₹ 166
(D) ₹ 278

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

Option A: Added $3(8)$ instead of subtracting: $512 + 24 = 536$ or rounded to 570.

✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Apply expansion $(x + 1/x)^3 - 3(x + 1/x) = 8^3 - 3(8) = 512 - 24 = 488$

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
$488 + 3(8) = 488 + 24 = 512 = 8^3$. Identity holds identically.
Using the cubic identity:
$x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)$
Given $x + \frac{1}{x} = 8$:
$x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 8^3 - 3(8) = 512 - 24 = 488$.
The amount spent by Gita is ₹ 488.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — ₹ 488

Q96. Parallelogram Diagonal Bisectors and Midpoint Concurrency Truth Analysis

💎 HOTS · ACHIEVERS SECTION (3 MARKS) D4 QRT-JUSTIFY-D4 📚 Quadrilaterals 📄 2025-26 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Achievers Section · Question 46 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q046)
💎 Achievers Section · HOTS Multi-Stage Synthesis Demands coordinating multiple geometric/algebraic invariants with rigorous justification. Weightage: 3 Marks · Demand: JUSTIFY.
Official Exam Question:
Read the given statements carefully and select the correct option.
Statement-I : $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. If $L$ and $M$ are points on $AB$ and $DC$ respectively and $AL = CM$, then $LM$ and $BD$ bisect each other.
Statement-II : $P$ is the mid-point of side $AB$ of a parallelogram $ABCD$. If a line through $B$ parallel to $PD$ meets $DC$ at $Q$ and $AD$ produced at $R$, then $AR = BC$ and $BR = 3BQ$.
(A) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
(B) Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
(C) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
(D) Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Parallelogram Diagonal Bisectors and Midpoint Concurrency Truth Analysis

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

For Statement I: $AB = CD$ and $AL = CM \implies BL = DM$. Since $BL \parallel DM$, what type of quadrilateral is $BLDM$?

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

For Statement II: In $\triangle ABR$, $P$ is midpoint of $AB$ and $PD \parallel BR$. By converse of mid-point theorem, $D$ is midpoint of $AR$. Does $AR = BC$?

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Falsely accepted Statement II without verifying segment length doubling.
Option C: Failed to identify that $BLDM$ forms a parallelogram in Statement I.
Option D: Inverted truth evaluations.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Prove Statement I true by parallelogram $BLDM$ diagonals bisecting, and disprove Statement II because $D$ is midpoint of $AR \implies AR = 2AD = 2BC \ne BC$

✓ Formal Verification (ALTERNATE_METHOD)
Coordinate geometry check: Let $A=(0,0), B=(2,0), D=(0,2) \implies C=(2,2)$. $P=(1,0)$. Line $PD$ slope is $-2$. Line through $B(2,0)$ parallel to $PD$ is $y - 0 = -2(x - 2) \implies y = -2x + 4$. Line $AD$ produced is x=0 (y-axis). Intersection $R=(0,4)$. Then $AR = 4$, while $BC = AD = 2$. $AR = 2BC \ne BC$. Statement II is unequivocally false.
Analysis of Statement-I:
In parallelogram $ABCD$, $AB = CD$ and $AB \parallel CD$.
Given $AL = CM$, we have $BL = AB - AL = CD - CM = DM$.
Since $BL = DM$ and $BL \parallel DM$, quadrilateral $BLDM$ is a parallelogram.
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other; hence $LM$ and $BD$ bisect each other.
Statement-I is TRUE.

Analysis of Statement-II:
In $\triangle ABR$, $P$ is the midpoint of $AB$, and $PD \parallel BR$.
By the converse of the mid-point theorem, $D$ must be the midpoint of side $AR$.
Thus $AR = 2 AD$. In parallelogram $ABCD$, $AD = BC$.
Therefore $AR = 2 BC \ne BC$.
Since the statement asserts $AR = BC$, Statement-II is FALSE.

Conclusion: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.

Part (i): $1500\sqrt{3} \approx 2598.076$. $s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c) = 150*90*50*10 = 6750000 = (1500)^2 * 3$. Exact.
Part (ii): $16^2 * \sqrt{3}/4 = 256/4 * \sqrt{3} = 64\sqrt{3}$. Exact.
Part (i):

$3x + 5x + 7x = 15x = 300 \implies x = 20\text{ m}$.
Sides: $a = 60\text{ m}, b = 100\text{ m}, c = 140\text{ m}$.
Semi-perimeter $s = 300 / 2 = 150\text{ m}$.
By Heron's Formula:
$\text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{150(150-60)(150-100)(150-140)}$
$= \sqrt{150 \times 90 \times 50 \times 10} = \sqrt{(150 \times 50) \times (90 \times 10)} = \sqrt{7500 \times 900} = \sqrt{6750000} = 1500\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^2$.

$\text{Area}_{\text{tri}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} s_{\text{tri}}^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (16)^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (256) = 64\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.

Q99. Truth Value Assessment of Algebraic Surds and Reciprocal Identities

💎 HOTS · ACHIEVERS SECTION (3 MARKS) D4 QRT-JUSTIFY-D4 📚 Number Systems 📄 2025-26 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Achievers Section · Question 49 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q049)
💎 Achievers Section · HOTS Multi-Stage Synthesis Demands coordinating multiple geometric/algebraic invariants with rigorous justification. Weightage: 3 Marks · Demand: JUSTIFY.
Official Exam Question:
Read the given statements carefully and state T for true and F for false.
(i) If $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = 3$, then the value of $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3}$ is equal to $3\sqrt{3}$.
(ii) If $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} = 27$, then the value of $x + \frac{1}{x}$ and $x - \frac{1}{x}$ are respectively 25 and 10.
(iii) If $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}$, then the value of $x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3$ is 4.
(A) (i) F, (ii) T, (iii) T
(B) (i) F, (ii) F, (iii) T
(C) (i) T, (ii) F, (iii) F
(D) (i) T, (ii) T, (iii) F
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Truth Value Assessment of Algebraic Surds and Reciprocal Identities

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

For (i): $x + 1/x = \sqrt{3}$. Use $(x+1/x)^3 - 3(x+1/x) = (\sqrt{3})^3 - 3\sqrt{3}$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

For (ii): $(x + 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 + 2 = 27 + 2 = 29 \implies x + 1/x = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$. For (iii): Rationalize $x = \sqrt{5} + 2 \implies (x - 2)^2 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0$.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed statement (ii) is true by omitting square root ($25$).
Option C: Assumed statement (i) is true by omitting $-3(x+1/x)$ subtraction.
Option D: Inverted truth assignment.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Prove (i) False ($x^3+1/x^3 = 0$), (ii) False ($x+1/x = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$), (iii) True ($x^2-4x-1=0 \implies P(x) = 4$); output (F, F, T)

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
Compute (iii) directly: $\sqrt{5}+2 \approx 4.236068$. $x^3 = (2+\sqrt{5})^3 = 8 + 12\sqrt{5} + 30 + 5\sqrt{5} = 38 + 17\sqrt{5}$. $-3x^2 = -3(9+4\sqrt{5}) = -27 - 12\sqrt{5}$. $-5x = -10 - 5\sqrt{5}$. $+3 = +3$. Sum: $(38 - 27 - 10 + 3) + (17 - 12 - 5)\sqrt{5} = 4 + 0\sqrt{5} = 4$. Exact match!
Statement (i):
Given $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = 3 \implies x + \frac{1}{x} = \pm\sqrt{3}$.
$x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right) = (\pm\sqrt{3})^3 - 3(\pm\sqrt{3}) = \pm 3\sqrt{3} \mp 3\sqrt{3} = 0$.
The statement claims the value is $3\sqrt{3}$, which is FALSE (F).

Statement (ii):
$\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} + 2 = 27 + 2 = 29 \implies x + \frac{1}{x} = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$.
$\left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} - 2 = 27 - 2 = 25 \implies x - \frac{1}{x} = 5 \ne 10$.
Statement (ii) is FALSE (F).

Statement (iii):
$x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2} = \frac{\sqrt{5}+2}{5-4} = \sqrt{5} + 2$.
$x - 2 = \sqrt{5} \implies (x - 2)^2 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x + 4 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0$.
Dividing $x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3$ by $x^2 - 4x - 1$:
$x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3 = (x + 1)(x^2 - 4x - 1) + 4 = (x + 1)(0) + 4 = 4$.
Statement (iii) is TRUE (T).

Result: (F, F, T) (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — (i) F, (ii) F, (iii) T

Q100. Circle Central Angle, Cyclic Quadrilateral Invariant, and Parallel Chord Scale

💎 HOTS · ACHIEVERS SECTION (3 MARKS) D4 QRT-SYNTHESIZE-D4 📚 Circles 📄 2025-26 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Achievers Section · Question 50 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q050)
💎 Achievers Section · HOTS Multi-Stage Synthesis Demands coordinating multiple geometric/algebraic invariants with rigorous justification. Weightage: 3 Marks · Demand: SYNTHESIZE.
Official Exam Question:
Fill in the blanks and select the correct option.

(ii) If the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is $180^\circ$, then the quadrilateral is ______.
(iii) In the given figure (not drawn to scale), chord $ED$ is parallel to the diameter $AC$ of the circle. Given $\angle CBE = 25^\circ$. If $\angle DEC = \frac{1}{k} \times 455^\circ$, then the value of $k$ is ______.
Figure: Official Vector Geometry (FIG-IMO-G09-2025-26-B-Q050.svg)
(A) (i) 7, (ii) trapezium, (iii) 5
(B) (i) 3, (ii) cyclic, (iii) 7
(C) (i) 3, (ii) trapezium, (iii) 7
(D) (i) 3, (ii) cyclic, (iii) 5
Target Mathematical Act (SYNTHESIZE): Circle Central Angle, Cyclic Quadrilateral Invariant, and Parallel Chord Scale

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

For (ii): By Euclid and circle theorems, a quadrilateral whose opposite angles sum to $180^\circ$ is cyclic.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

For (iii): $AC$ is diameter $\implies \angle AEC = 90^\circ$. $\angle CAE = \angle CBE = 25^\circ$. In $\triangle AEC$, $\angle ECA = 90^\circ - 25^\circ = 65^\circ$. Since $ED \parallel AC$, $\angle DEC = \angle ECA = 65^\circ$. Solve $65 = 455/k$.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed quadrilateral is a trapezium and miscalculated $k=5$.
Option C: Labelled quadrilateral as trapezium instead of cyclic.
Option D: Miscalculated $k=5$ ($5 \times 65 = 325 \ne 455$).
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Part (i): central angle evaluation gives 3; Part (ii): opposite angle supplementary property defines 'cyclic'; Part (iii): diameter semicircle $90^\circ$ plus parallel chord gives $65^\circ = 455^\circ / k \implies k = 7$

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
$7 \times 65 = 455$. Angle in semicircle $= 90^\circ$. Opposite angles $= 180^\circ$ defines cyclic quadrilateral. Exact.
Part (i):
With $\angle CEA = 30^\circ$ inscribed on diameter/chord $AC$, evaluating central angle and subtended angular differences gives $(x - y - z) = 60^\circ$.
$\frac{x - y - z}{20^\circ} = \frac{60^\circ}{20^\circ} = 3$.

Part (ii):
By the converse of the cyclic quadrilateral theorem (NCERT Theorem 9.12), if the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is $180^\circ$, the quadrilateral is CYCLIC.

Part (iii):
$AC$ is the diameter $\implies \angle AEC = 90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle).
Angles in the same segment: $\angle CAE = \angle CBE = 25^\circ$.
In right triangle $\triangle AEC$:
$\angle ECA = 180^\circ - (90^\circ + 25^\circ) = 65^\circ$.
Since chord $ED \parallel \text{diameter } AC$, alternate interior angles are equal:
$\angle DEC = \angle ECA = 65^\circ$.
Given $\angle DEC = \frac{1}{k} \times 455^\circ$:
$65^\circ = \frac{455^\circ}{k} \implies k = \frac{455}{65} = 7$.

Combined tuple: (3, cyclic, 7) (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — (i) 3, (ii) cyclic, (iii) 7

Q131. Euclidean Subtraction Axiom on Collinear Line Segments

(A) PQ = QR
(B) PQ = RS
(C) QR = RS
(D) PR = RS
Target Mathematical Act (RETRIEVE): Euclidean Subtraction Axiom on Collinear Line Segments

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Notice that segment QR is common to both PR and QS: PR = PQ + QR and QS = QR + RS.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Subtract the common segment QR from both sides of PR = QS: PR - QR = QS - QR.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumes Q is midpoint of PR.
Option C: Assumes QR equals RS.
Option D: Conflates whole with part.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Invoke Euclid's Axiom 3 (equals subtracted from equals are equal): PR = QS => PR - QR = QS - QR => PQ = RS

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Collinear coordinates: P=0, Q=3, R=7, S=10. PR = 7 - 0 = 7. QS = 10 - 3 = 7. PQ = 3 - 0 = 3. RS = 10 - 7 = 3. PQ = RS. Holds.
Points P, Q, R, S lie in that order on a line segment. 1) PR = PQ + QR. 2) QS = QR + RS. 3) Given PR = QS => PQ + QR = QR + RS. 4) By Euclid's Axiom 3: 'If equals are subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal.' Subtracting QR from both sides: (PQ + QR) - QR = (QR + RS) - QR => PQ = RS. Therefore, PQ = RS (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — PQ = RS

Q132. Parallelogram Interior Angle Bisector Enclosure Theorem

D2 QRT-JUSTIFY-D2 📚 Quadrilaterals 📄 2024-25 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2024-25-B · Mathematical Reasoning · Question 32 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2024-25-B-Q032)
Official Exam Question:
The quadrilateral formed by the bisectors of the interior angles of a parallelogram is a:
(A) Square
(B) Rectangle
(C) Rhombus
(D) Trapezium
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Parallelogram Interior Angle Bisector Enclosure Theorem

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary (sum = 180°). What is the sum of their halves?

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

In Δ formed by bisectors of adjacent angles A and B: (1/2)∠A + (1/2)∠B = (1/2)(180°) = 90°. Hence the third angle is 180° - 90° = 90°. All 4 angles are 90°.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: A square requires all four sides to be equal, which is not true unless the original parallelogram is a rhombus.
Option C: A rhombus requires equal sides with non-right angles generally.
Option D: A trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Adjacent angles of parallelogram sum to 180° => their half-angles sum to 90° => bisectors meet at 90° at all 4 vertices, forming a rectangle

✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE)
Standard NCERT Theorem 8.4: Bisectors of interior angles of a parallelogram enclose a rectangle. Valid.
Let ABCD be a parallelogram. 1) Adjacent angles are supplementary: ∠A + ∠B = 180°. 2) The angle bisectors divide these angles into (1/2)∠A and (1/2)∠B. In the triangle formed by these bisectors and side AB, the sum of base angles is (1/2)∠A + (1/2)∠B = (1/2)(∠A + ∠B) = (1/2)(180°) = 90°. 3) Therefore, the vertex angle of intersection = 180° - 90° = 90°. 4) Repeating for all four pairs of adjacent angles proves that each interior angle of the enclosed quadrilateral is 90°. A quadrilateral with all four interior angles equal to 90° is a rectangle. Therefore, the enclosed figure is a rectangle (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — Rectangle

By the Factor Theorem, (x - 1) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(1) = 0. P(1) = k(1)² - √2(1) + 1 = 0 => k - √2 + 1 = 0 => k = √2 - 1. Therefore, k = √2 - 1 (Option A).

Q135. Heron's Formula Variable Side-Length Area Derivation

D2 QRT-APPLY-D2 📚 Heron's Formula and Surface Area 📄 2024-25 Set B 📖 Core 1A/1B

The perimeter of a triangle is 50 cm. One side of the triangle is 4 cm longer than the smallest side and the third side is 6 cm less than twice the smallest side. Find the area of the triangle.
Figure: Triangle $ABC$ with sides $13\\text{ cm}, 17\\text{ cm}, 20\\text{ cm}$ (2024-25 Set B, Q35)
(A) 20√30 cm²
(B) 25√30 cm²
(C) 30√20 cm²
(D) 15√30 cm²
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Heron's Formula Variable Side-Length Area Derivation

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Let the smallest side be s. Express the other two sides in terms of s and use the perimeter 50 cm to solve for s.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Sides are s, s + 4, and 2s - 6. Sum: 4s - 2 = 50 => s = 13. Sides are 13, 17, 20. Use Heron's formula with semiperimeter = 25.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option B: Calculated 25√30 cm².
Option C: Inverted factors to 30√20 cm².
Option D: Arithmetic error yielding 15√30 cm².
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Solve perimeter s + (s+4) + (2s-6) = 50 => 4s - 2 = 50 => s = 13; evaluate sides 13, 17, 20 with semiperimeter 25 to get 20√30 cm²

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
25 × 12 × 8 × 5 = 12000. 20² × 30 = 400 × 30 = 12000. √12000 = 20√30 cm². Exact match to Option A.
1) Let smallest side be a = s. Then side b = s + 4, and side c = 2s - 6. 2) Perimeter = a + b + c = s + (s + 4) + (2s - 6) = 4s - 2. Given perimeter = 50 cm => 4s - 2 = 50 => 4s = 52 => s = 13 cm. 3) The three sides are: a = 13 cm, b = 13 + 4 = 17 cm, c = 2(13) - 6 = 26 - 6 = 20 cm. Check: 13 + 17 + 20 = 50 cm. 4) Semiperimeter s_p = 50 / 2 = 25 cm. 5) By Heron's formula: Area = √[s_p(s_p - a)(s_p - b)(s_p - c)] = √[25(25 - 13)(25 - 17)(25 - 20)] = √[25 × 12 × 8 × 5] = √[25 × (4 × 3) × (4 × 2) × 5] = √[25 × 16 × 30] = 5 × 4 × √30 = 20√30 cm² (Option A).
Verified Answer: Option (A) — 20√30 cm²

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

P(1)=0, P(2)=0, P(3)=0 confirms roots. P(4)=6 confirms remainder. Both statements true. Option C is exact.
1) Proof of Statement-I: Expand (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3): (x - 1)(x - 2) = x² - 3x + 2. (x² - 3x + 2)(x - 3) = x³ - 3x² - 3x² + 9x + 2x - 6 = x³ - 6x² + 11x - 6 = P(x). Therefore, (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3) is the exact factorization. Statement-I is TRUE. 2) Proof of Statement-II: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder when P(x) is divided by (x - 4) is P(4). Using the factored form: P(4) = (4 - 1)(4 - 2)(4 - 3) = 3 × 2 × 1 = 6. Alternatively: 4³ - 6(4²) + 11(4) - 6 = 64 - 96 + 44 - 6 = 108 - 102 = 6. Therefore, Statement-II is TRUE. Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true, corresponding to Option C.

5. In ∆ADE, two angles are equal (∠ADE = ∠DAE). Therefore, the sides opposite to equal angles must be equal: AE = ED.
6. Hence, ∆ADE is an isosceles triangle with AE = ED.

1. Volume of cone V = (1/3)π r² h.
2. Ratio of volumes: V₁ / V₂ = (r₁² · h₁) / (r₂² · h₂) = (r₁ / r₂)² · (h₁ / h₂).
3. Given: r₁ / r₂ = 2 / 3 and V₁ / V₂ = 4 / 5.
4. Substitute: 4 / 5 = (2 / 3)² · (h₁ / h₂) = (4 / 9) · (h₁ / h₂).
5. Multiply both sides by 9 / 4: h₁ / h₂ = (4 / 5) · (9 / 4) = 9 / 5.
6. Therefore, the ratio of their heights is 9 : 5.

(B) 5 - 2√6
(C) -(5 + 2√6)
(D) 2√6 - 5
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Additive Inverse of Compound Rational Surd Expression

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

First simplify the given surd expression by rationalising its denominator.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Multiply numerator and denominator by (√3 + √2). The additive inverse of the resulting value A is -A.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Gave the value of X itself without taking the additive inverse.
Option B: Took the conjugate 5 - 2√6 instead of the additive inverse.
Option D: Changed the sign of only the integer part: 2√6 - 5.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Additive inverse of X is -X. Rationalise denominators and evaluate exact opposite sign

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
X + (-X) = (5 + 2√6) + [-(5 + 2√6)] = 0. The definition of additive inverse is satisfied identically. Option C verified.
1. Simplify the given expression:
X = (√3 + √2) / (√3 - √2)
2. Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (√3 + √2):
X = (√3 + √2)² / [(√3 - √2)(√3 + √2)]
3. Denominator = (√3)² - (√2)² = 3 - 2 = 1.
4. Numerator = (√3)² + 2(√3)(√2) + (√2)² = 3 + 2√6 + 2 = 5 + 2√6.
5. Therefore, X = 5 + 2√6.
6. The additive inverse of X is -X = -(5 + 2√6) = -5 - 2√6.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — -(5 + 2√6)

(B) Rhombus

(D) Trapezium

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed all sides are equal (square), which only occurs if transversal is perpendicular.
Option B: Confused 90° angles with equal side lengths (rhombus).

✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Consecutive interior angles sum to 180°. Their bisectors meet at 90°. All 4 interior angles of the formed quadrilateral are 90°, proving it is a rectangle

✓ Formal Verification (GEOMETRIC_INVARIANT_CHECK)
All 4 internal angles = 90° forces a rectangle. Equilateral property (square/rhombus) only holds when transversal is perpendicular, not in general. Option C is the canonical geometric theorem.
1. Let parallel lines AB and CD be intersected by transversal EF at points P and Q.
2. Consecutive interior angles on the same side sum to 180°: ∠BPQ + ∠PQD = 180°.
3. The bisectors of ∠BPQ and ∠PQD meet at R. In ∆PQR: ∠RPQ = (1/2)∠BPQ and ∠PQR = (1/2)∠PQD.
4. Therefore: ∠RPQ + ∠PQR = (1/2)(∠BPQ + ∠PQD) = (1/2)(180°) = 90°.
5. In ∆PQR, sum of angles is 180°, so ∠PRQ = 180° - 90° = 90°.
6. By the exact same reasoning on the other side and at all 4 vertices, every interior angle of the enclosed quadrilateral measures 90°.
7. A quadrilateral whose all four interior angles are 90° is a rectangle. (It cannot be guaranteed to be a square because adjacent side lengths depend on the transversal angle and line distance).
Verified Answer: Option (C) — Rectangle

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

Option A: Failed to distribute negative sign to the x² and constant terms: 2x³ + 5x² - 7x + 11.
Option B: Added the two polynomials together instead of subtracting: 4x³ + x² + 3x - 3.
Option D: Subtracted in reverse order (B - A): -2x³ + 5x² - 7x + 11.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Subtracting P from Q means computing Q - P. Distribute negative sign across all terms of P and combine like terms

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
(3x³ - 2x² + 5x - 7) - (2x³ - 5x² + 7x - 11) = (3-2)x³ + (-2 - (-5))x² + (5-7)x + (-7 - (-11)) = x³ + 3x² - 2x + 4. Matches target identically. Option C verified.
1. Let the required polynomial be P.
(3x³ - 2x² + 5x - 7) - P = (x³ + 3x² - 2x + 4)
2. P = (3x³ - 2x² + 5x - 7) - (x³ + 3x² - 2x + 4)
3. Distribute the minus sign:
P = 3x³ - 2x² + 5x - 7 - x³ - 3x² + 2x - 4
4. Group like terms:
x³ terms: 3x³ - x³ = 2x³
x² terms: -2x² - 3x² = -5x²
x terms: 5x + 2x = 7x
Constant terms: -7 - 4 = -11
5. Therefore, P = 2x³ - 5x² + 7x - 11.
Verified Answer: Option (C) — 2x³ - 5x² + 7x - 11

2. Heron's formula:

Area = √[21 · (21 - 13) · (21 - 14) · (21 - 15)]
Area = √[21 · 8 · 7 · 6]

Area = √(2⁴ · 3² · 7²) = 2² · 3 · 7 = 4 · 21 = 84 cm².

h = 84 / 7 = 12 cm.

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
P = 4460. After 3 years: 4460 * (3/2) = 6690. After 6 years: 6690 * (3/2) = 10035. Equations satisfied exactly. Option A verified.
1. Let principal be P and annual compound interest factor be k = (1 + r/100)³.
2. After 3 years: P · k = 6690 --- (Eq 1)
3. After 6 years: P · k² = 10035 --- (Eq 2)
4. Divide Eq 2 by Eq 1:
(P · k²) / (P · k) = 10035 / 6690
k = 10035 / 6690
Divide numerator and denominator by 3345:
10035 / 3345 = 3
6690 / 3345 = 2
Therefore, k = 3 / 2.
5. Substitute k = 3/2 into Eq 1:
P · (3/2) = 6690
P = 6690 · (2/3) = 2230 · 2 = ₹ 4,460.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — ₹ 4,460

Q186. Combined Harmonic Work Rate for Two Agents

Official Exam Question:
A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B can do the same work in 15 days. In how many days can both of them together complete the same work?
(A) 6 days
(B) 8 days
(C) 5 days
(D) 7 days
Target Mathematical Act (MODEL): Combined Harmonic Work Rate for Two Agents

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Find the work done by A and B in 1 day individually.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

A's 1-day work = 1/10; B's 1-day work = 1/15. Add them together: 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6. Invert to get total days.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option B: Averaged the days: (10 + 15)/2 = 12.5, or estimated 8 days.
Option C: Subtracted rates: 15 - 10 = 5 days.
Option D: Arithmetic estimation slip: 7 days.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Combined work rate = 1/A + 1/B. Total time T = 1 / (1/A + 1/B) = (A * B) / (A + B)

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
In 6 days: A completes 6/10 = 3/5; B completes 6/15 = 2/5. Total work = 3/5 + 2/5 = 5/5 = 1 (complete work). Option A verified.
1. Work done by A in 1 day = 1/10.
2. Work done by B in 1 day = 1/15.
3. Work done by (A + B) together in 1 day = 1/10 + 1/15.
LCM of 10 and 15 is 30.
(3 + 2) / 30 = 5 / 30 = 1/6.
4. Therefore, total time taken by both together to complete the work = 1 / (1/6) = 6 days.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — 6 days

Q187. Multi-Stage Percentage Population Inversion

(B) 95,000
(C) 98,000
(D) 1,00,000
Target Mathematical Act (MODEL): Multi-Stage Percentage Population Inversion

💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Let the original population 2 years ago be P. Apply successive percentage reductions.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

After year 1: P · (1 - 0.10) = 0.90 P. After year 2: 0.90 P · (1 - 0.20) = 0.72 P. Set 0.72 P = 72,000 and solve for P.

The decisive move and full worked check become available only after you commit your own working.

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Simply added 10% + 20% = 30% to 72,000: 72,000 * 1.30 = 93,600, or assumed 90,000.
Option B: Calculated 72,000 / (1 - 0.30) ≈ 1,02,857, rounded to 95,000.
Option C: Applied one reduction stage only.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Available after a committed attempt
⚡ Key Olympiad Invariant / Crux Move

Formulate consecutive percentage decrements: remaining population P * (1 - d_1) * (1 - d_2) = final count. Solve for P

✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK)
1,00,000 - 10% (10,000) = 90,000. 90,000 - 20% (18,000) = 72,000. Matches present population. Option D verified.
1. Let the population of the town 2 years ago be P.
2. Decrease in year 1 = 10%, so population after year 1 = P · (1 - 10/100) = 0.9 P.
3. Decrease in year 2 = 20%, so population after year 2 = (0.9 P) · (1 - 20/100) = 0.9 P · 0.8 = 0.72 P.
4. Given present population = 72,000:
0.72 P = 72,000
P = 72,000 / 0.72 = 1,00,000.
5. Therefore, the population 2 years ago was 1,00,000.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — 1,00,000

Q188. Affine Taxi Fare Model with Fixed Charge and Variable Distance
