Circles and Cyclic Quadrilaterals

Mathematical Domain: Euclidean Plane Geometry (R^2)
🔗 Anchored to 2 Authenticated Core 2 Questions (Click to expand list)
SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q050SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q050
BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Familiarity with inscribed angles and central angle subtension theorems in a single circle.
  • Understanding of supplementary angles along a straight line (linear pairs) and parallel line angle criteria.
Hypotheses:
  • Quadrilateral ABCD is cyclic with all four vertices on circle C_1.
  • Circle C_2 passes through vertices A and B, intersecting secant line AD at point E and secant line BC at point F.
  • Points A, E, D are distinct and collinear in order A-E-D.
  • Points B, F, C are distinct and collinear in order B-F-C.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Degenerate circles of radius zero.
  • Collinear vertex configurations (triangle degeneracies).
  • Tangent contact where E coincides with A or F coincides with B.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why the angle subtended by an arc at the circumference is half the central angle, forcing opposite angles of any cyclic quadrilateral to sum to 180 degrees, and how chaining this supplementary invariant across intersecting circles transfers equal corresponding angles to force two chords to be strictly parallel.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

In any cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of either pair of opposite angles is 180 degrees.

Let arc BCD subtend central angle alpha at O, and arc BAD subtend reflex central angle beta. Then alpha + beta = 360 deg. By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, angle(BAD) = beta / 2 and angle(BCD) = alpha / 2. Therefore, angle(BAD) + angle(BCD) = (alpha + beta) / 2 = 360 / 2 = 180 deg.

✅ Why valid: Every point on circle C_1 belongs to either the major or minor arc; their central angles partition the full circle of 360 degrees.

STEP-02 WARRANT

The exterior angle formed by producing a side of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.

In cyclic quad ABFE (in circle C_2), angle(ABF) + angle(AEF) = 180 deg. Since A-E-D is a straight line segment, angle(AEF) + angle(DEF) = 180 deg (linear pair). Subtracting gives angle(DEF) = angle(ABF).

✅ Why valid: Angles supplementary to the exact same angle are strictly equal to each other.

STEP-03 WARRANT

In outer circle C_1, cyclic quadrilateral ABCD gives angle(BCD) = 180 deg - angle(BAD) and angle(CDE) = angle(ABF).

In cyclic quad ABCD, angle(BAD) + angle(BCD) = 180 deg, and along line B-F-C, angle(ABF) + angle(ADC) = 180 deg. Producing AD shows the exterior angle at D equals angle(ABF).

✅ Why valid: Vertices A, B, C, D lie on circle C_1, so the identical cyclic opposite-angle theorem applies.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Line segment EF is strictly parallel to chord DC.

From Step 2, angle(DEF) = angle(ABF). From Step 3, angle(CDE) = 180 deg - angle(ABF), so angle(DEF) + angle(CDE) = angle(ABF) + (180 deg - angle(ABF)) = 180 deg. For lines EF and DC intersected by transversal AD, consecutive interior angles angle(DEF) and angle(CDE) sum to 180 deg. By Euclid's converse of the parallel transversal theorem, EF is parallel to DC.

✅ Why valid: When consecutive interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary, the lines cannot intersect and are parallel.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

VISUAL_PARALLEL_ASSUMPTION Fallacy: Assuming chords EF and DC must be parallel because the figure looks symmetrical, without referencing cyclic quadrilateral angles.

Diagnostic Context: If circle C_2 passed through vertices A and D instead of A and B, would line EF still be parallel to DC?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Trace the exact circle containing quadrilateral ABFE. The parallelism requires vertices A and B to be shared by both circles; changing the intersection points changes the angle transfer and destroys parallelism.
OPPOSITE_EQUAL_CONFUSION Fallacy: Confusing cyclic quadrilaterals with parallelograms and assuming opposite angles are equal rather than supplementary.

Diagnostic Context: In a cyclic quadrilateral with one angle measuring 110 degrees, what is the opposite angle?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Remember: in parallelograms opposite angles are equal (110 = 110); in cyclic quadrilaterals opposite angles are supplementary (180 - 110 = 70 degrees).

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

Let two circles intersect at points A and B. Through A and B, two straight lines are drawn meeting the first circle at C, D and the second circle at E, F. Prove that CD is parallel to EF.

In the first circle, cyclic quad ABDC gives angle(BAC) + angle(BDC) = 180 deg. Along straight line CAE, angle(BAC) + angle(BAE) = 180 deg, so angle(BDC) = angle(BAE). In the second circle, cyclic quad ABFE gives angle(BAE) + angle(BFE) = 180 deg. Substituting angle(BAE) = angle(BDC) yields angle(BDC) + angle(BFE) = 180 deg. For lines CD and EF intersected by transversal DF, consecutive interior angles are supplementary. Hence, CD || EF.

🎯 Independent Exit Task (Technique T12)

In circle C_1, quadrilateral ABCD is cyclic. A second circle C_2 passes through C and D, meeting diagonal AC at P and diagonal BD at Q. Show that PQ is parallel to AB.

Reveal Model Exit Solution
In circle C_1, inscribed angles subtended by chord AB are equal: angle(ACB) = angle(ADB), so angle(PCD) = angle(QDC)... In circle C_2, cyclic quad CDQP has opposite angles supplementary, which transfers to corresponding angles equal: angle(CPQ) = angle(CAB). Therefore, PQ is parallel to AB.
BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1B-RECONSTRUCTION

Core 1B · Dual-Stage Recall & 4-Stage Self-Tutor Flow

Complete the four unassisted retrieval gates to lock in procedural and conceptual mastery without teacher deferral.

STAGE 1 · PREDICT GATE UNASSISTED RECALL

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Forces the learner to identify the topological membership of the two quadrilaterals in their respective circles before guessing parallelism.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

Formulate the exact chain of two angle equalities that connects angle(ABF) to angle(DEF) and to angle(CDE), and state which parallel-line condition this satisfies.

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: In circle C_2: quadrilateral ABFE is cyclic, so angle(DEF) = angle(ABF) (exterior angle equals interior opposite).
step_2: In circle C_1: quadrilateral ABCD is cyclic, so opposite angles are supplementary: angle(ADC) + angle(ABF) = 180 deg.
step_3: Substitute angle(ABF) = angle(DEF): angle(ADC) + angle(DEF) = 180 deg.
conclusion: Since consecutive interior angles on the same side of transversal AD sum to 180 deg, chord EF is parallel to chord DC.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION REVERSE_ENGINEERING_FROM_GOAL

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Suppose you are told EF is parallel to DC. Working BACKWARDS from the goal, what angle relationship between lines EF and DC across transversal AD would guarantee this?

Key Invariant Insight: Either corresponding angles are equal (angle AEF = angle ADC if produced), or consecutive interior angles are supplementary (angle DEF + angle ADC = 180 deg).

💬 Inquiry: Now look at angle ADC in outer circle C_1. What single angle in the diagram determines angle ADC?

Key Invariant Insight: The opposite angle in cyclic quad ABCD, which is angle ABC (or angle ABF).

💬 Inquiry: Finally, look at angle DEF. How does inner circle C_2 connect angle DEF to that exact same angle ABF?

Key Invariant Insight: Because ABFE is cyclic in C_2, its exterior angle DEF must equal interior opposite angle ABF. The two independent circle constraints meet at the shared angle ABF!

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: Suppose circle C_2 is continuously dilated until it coincides identically with circle C_1. What happens to points E and F, what does chord EF become, and does the parallel property still hold?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (B): At the boundary limit C_2 -> C_1, the secant intersection points E and F coincide with the outer circle endpoints D and C. The chord EF collapses onto DC. Every continuous perturbation preserves the angle invariant, confirming that the parallelism is robust and topologically intrinsic.

💡 2-Rung Scaffold Ladder (Non-Leaking Cognitive Anchors)

RUNG 1 · CONCEPTUAL NUDGE

Notice that vertices A and B belong to BOTH circles simultaneously. Find an angle at vertex B that serves as the bridge between outer quadrilateral ABCD and inner quadrilateral ABFE.

RUNG 2 · TACTICAL STEP

Write down the cyclic quadrilateral exterior angle theorem for quad ABFE: angle(DEF) = angle(ABF). Then write the cyclic opposite-angle sum for quad ABCD: angle(ADC) + angle(ABF) = 180 deg. Combine them to find the sum of angle(DEF) and angle(ADC).

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Mathematical Domain: Linear Systems over R and Geometric-Algebraic Consistency Classification
🔗 Anchored to 1 Authenticated Core 2 Questions (Click to expand list)
SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2024-25-B-Q050
BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Understanding of general bivariate linear equations in standard form a*x + b*y + c = 0.
  • Geometric interpretation of a linear equation as a straight line in the Cartesian plane R^2.
  • Basic mastery of ratio equality and the matrix determinant test for 2x2 linear systems.
Hypotheses:
  • Let L1: a1*x + b1*y = c1 and L2: a2*x + b2*y = c2 be two lines in R^2 with (a1^2 + b1^2 != 0) and (a2^2 + b2^2 != 0).
  • The normal vectors are n1 = (a1, b1) and n2 = (a2, b2).
  • Condition for Unique Solution: n1 and n2 are linearly independent, i.e., a1/a2 != b1/b2 (or a1*b2 - a2*b1 != 0).
  • Condition for Infinitely Many Solutions (Coincident): a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 (proportional lines).
  • Condition for Inconsistent System (Parallel, No Solution): a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 (equal slope, distinct intercepts).
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Zero denominators in ratio checks (treated by equivalent cross-multiplication form a1*b2 - a2*b1 = 0).
  • Assuming a system with a1/a2 = b1/b2 has solutions without verifying the constant term ratio c1/c2.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why comparing the coefficient ratios a1/a2, b1/b2, and c1/c2 rigorously determines the geometric configuration (intersecting, parallel, or coincident) and algebraic solvability (unique, inconsistent, or infinitely many solutions) without requiring explicit variable elimination.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Transform both equations into standard bivariate linear form: a1*x + b1*y = c1 and a2*x + b2*y = c2.

Identify the coefficient tuple (a1, b1, c1) and (a2, b2, c2) ensuring sign preservation.

✅ Why valid: Linear equations are uniquely defined up to scalar multiplication by their Cartesian coefficients.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Formulate the cross-multiplication determinant Delta = a1*b2 - a2*b1.

From Cramer's rule, x = (c1*b2 - c2*b1)/Delta and y = (a1*c2 - a2*c1)/Delta.

✅ Why valid: Division by non-zero Delta guarantees a uniquely determined point (x, y) in the real plane R^2.

STEP-03 WARRANT

For a system to possess a unique solution, the necessary and sufficient condition is Delta != 0, which corresponds to a1/a2 != b1/b2.

If Delta = 0, the coefficient vector (a1, b1) is collinear with (a2, b2), meaning both lines share identical inclinations.

✅ Why valid: Lines with non-parallel directions must intersect at one and only one Euclidean point.

STEP-04 WARRANT

When a parameter k is present in b1 or b2, solve the inequality a1/a2 != b1/b2 to find the exact forbidden value of k.

Cross-multiplying a1*b2 != a2*b1 isolates k, yielding k != (a1*b2_alt)/a2.

✅ Why valid: The complementary set R \ {k_critical} represents all parameter choices maintaining linear independence.

📊 Topic Visual Representation & Invariant Diagram

Anchor: Invariant Vector Diagram

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

CONFUSING_INCONSISTENT_WITH_DEPENDENT Fallacy: Assuming a1/a2 = b1/b2 implies infinitely many solutions without checking the constant ratio c1/c2.

Diagnostic Context: If a1/a2 = b1/b2, can you immediately assert whether the system has no solution or infinitely many?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Equal coefficient ratios only prove parallelism. You must evaluate the constant term ratio: if != c1/c2 it is inconsistent (no solution); if == c1/c2 it is dependent (infinite solutions).
SIGN_ERROR_IN_NEGATIVE_COEFFICIENT_RATIO Fallacy: Ignoring negative signs when extracting b coefficients, e.g. treating 3x - 5y as b = +5.

Diagnostic Context: In the equation 3x - 5y = 7, what is the value of the y-coefficient b?

Refutation & Repair Rule: In standard form ax + by = c, the negative sign belongs to the coefficient: b = -5, so the ratio must carry the negative sign.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

Determine the value of m for which the system of linear equations 3x + my = 4 and 6x - 8y = 9 has: (i) a unique solution, and (ii) no solution.

Extract coefficients: a1 = 3, b1 = m, c1 = 4; a2 = 6, b2 = -8, c2 = 9. Ratio of x-coefficients: a1/a2 = 3/6 = 1/2. Ratio of y-coefficients: b1/b2 = m/(-8). Ratio of constants: c1/c2 = 4/9 != 1/2. (i) For a unique solution, a1/a2 != b1/b2 => 1/2 != m/(-8) => m != -4. Thus, the system has a unique solution for all real m != -4. (ii) For no solution, a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 => 1/2 = m/(-8) != 4/9 => m = -4. When m = -4, the lines are strictly parallel with no solution.

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Mathematical Domain: Coordinate Geometry and Bivariate Affine Locus Analysis

BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Definition of Cartesian coordinates: abscissa (x) and ordinate (y).
  • Standard form of linear equation in two variables: Ax + By = C.
  • Formulas for triangle area in R^2 and substitution of geometric constraints into algebraic loci.
Hypotheses:
  • Let L: Ax + By = C be a straight line with A != 0, B != 0, and C != 0.
  • The x-axis corresponds to the locus y = 0, intersecting L at (C/A, 0).
  • The y-axis corresponds to the locus x = 0, intersecting L at (0, C/B).
  • The triangle formed by L with the coordinate axes has vertices (0,0), (C/A, 0), and (0, C/B).
  • The diagonal bisector locus x = y intersects L at the unique point (C/(A+B), C/(A+B)).
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Lines passing through the origin (C = 0) where both intercepts degenerate into (0, 0).
  • Lines parallel to an axis (A = 0 or B = 0) where the intercept does not exist or triangle area is undefined.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why synthesizing the algebraic equation Ax + By = C across boundary planes (y=0, x=0, and y=x) reveals the complete geometric profile of the linear graph: the orthogonal intercept coordinates, the enclosed triangular area with the coordinate axes, and the diagonal intersection point.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Calculate the x-intercept by setting y = 0 in the equation Ax + By = C.

Ax + B(0) = C => Ax = C => x = C/A. Point is (C/A, 0).

✅ Why valid: Every point on the Cartesian x-axis has ordinate y = 0 by definition of the coordinate plane.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Calculate the y-intercept by setting x = 0 in the equation Ax + By = C.

A(0) + By = C => By = C => y = C/B. Point is (0, C/B).

✅ Why valid: Every point on the Cartesian y-axis has abscissa x = 0 by definition of the coordinate plane.

STEP-03 WARRANT

Compute the area of the right triangle enclosed between the line and the coordinate axes.

The coordinate axes are perpendicular, forming a right triangle with base |C/A| and height |C/B|. Area = (1/2) * |C/A| * |C/B| = C^2 / (2 * |A * B|).

✅ Why valid: Euclidean area of a right-angled triangle equals half the product of its orthogonal legs.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Determine the coordinates of the point on the line where abscissa equals ordinate.

Impose the constraint y = x: Ax + Bx = C => (A + B)x = C => x = C / (A + B). Ordinate is also y = C / (A + B).

✅ Why valid: Simultaneous intersection of the line Ax + By = C and the identity line y = x yields the unique equi-coordinate point.

📊 Topic Visual Representation & Invariant Diagram

🌉 Representation Bridge (Symbolic & Visual Mapping)

Anchor: Invariant Vector Diagram

The right-angled triangular region bounded by the line and both coordinate axes.
(x_d, y_d) = \left(\frac{C}{A+B}, \frac{C}{A+B}\right)
The unique point on the line lying on the identity ray where abscissa equals ordinate.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

ABSCISSA_ORDINATE_CONFUSION Fallacy: Swapping abscissa and ordinate, setting x = 0 for x-intercept or thinking abscissa is y.

Diagnostic Context: Which coordinate is the abscissa, and what is its value along the y-axis?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Abscissa is the x-coordinate (horizontal); ordinate is the y-coordinate (vertical). At the x-axis, y = 0.
NEGATIVE_AREA_FALLACY Fallacy: Leaving a negative sign in the area calculation when intercepts lie on negative axes.

Diagnostic Context: Can a geometric region have a negative area if an intercept is negative?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Area is strictly non-negative. Always take the absolute magnitude of lengths: Area = (1/2) * |x_int| * |y_int|.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

For the linear equation 4x + 5y = 20: (P) Find the x-intercept, (Q) Find the y-intercept, (R) Compute the area of the triangle formed with the axes, and (S) Find the point where abscissa equals ordinate.

1. x-intercept: Set y = 0 => 4x = 20 => x = 5. Coordinates: (5, 0).
2. y-intercept: Set x = 0 => 5y = 20 => y = 4. Coordinates: (0, 4).
3. Triangle area: Legs are 5 and 4. Area = (1/2) * 5 * 4 = 10 sq units.
4. Abscissa = ordinate: Set y = x => 4x + 5x = 20 => 9x = 20 => x = 20/9 ≈ 2.22. Point is (20/9, 20/9).

step_2: y-intercept: Set x = 0 => 4y = 24 => y = 6. Q is (0, 6).

Key Invariant Insight: The denominators a = C/A and b = C/B immediately yield the lengths of the x-intercept and y-intercept along the coordinate axes without separate substitution steps!

💬 Inquiry: How can you immediately write down the triangle area directly from the intercept form x/a + y/b = 1?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Every point on the x-axis has y = 0, and every point on the y-axis has x = 0. Substituting these zeroes isolates each intercept.

RUNG 2 · TACTICAL STEP

BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Expansion of binomial squares: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 and (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2.
  • Expansion of binomial cubes: (a + b)^3 = a^3 + b^3 + 3ab(a + b).
  • Conjugate rationalization of denominators containing radical binomials.
Hypotheses:
  • Let x be a non-zero real number with reciprocal 1/x.
  • The product x * (1/x) = 1 is invariant, linearizing cross-terms.
  • (x + 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 + 2 => x + 1/x = sqrt(x^2 + 1/x^2 + 2).
  • (x - 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 - 2 => x - 1/x = sqrt(x^2 + 1/x^2 - 2).
  • x^3 + 1/x^3 = (x + 1/x)^3 - 3*(x + 1/x).
  • If (x + 1/x)^2 = 3, then x^3 + 1/x^3 = (sqrt(3))^3 - 3*sqrt(3) = 0.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • x = 0 where reciprocal 1/x is undefined.
  • Assuming (x + 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 (Freshman's dream fallacy, omitting cross-term 2).
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why reciprocal symmetric pairings cancel the cross-term 2*x*(1/x) = 2, allowing powers of (x + 1/x) and (x - 1/x) to be computed deterministically from x^2 + 1/x^2 without ever solving for the underlying irrational root x.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Express the sum of cubes x^3 + 1/x^3 strictly in terms of the sum u = x + 1/x.

Expand (x + 1/x)^3 = x^3 + 1/x^3 + 3*x*(1/x)*(x + 1/x) = x^3 + 1/x^3 + 3(x + 1/x). Rearranging yields x^3 + 1/x^3 = u^3 - 3u.

✅ Why valid: Binomial expansion identity with reciprocal term cancellation x*(1/x) = 1.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Prove that if (x + 1/x)^2 = 3, then x^3 + 1/x^3 evaluates identically to 0.

If u^2 = 3, then u = ±sqrt(3). Then u^3 - 3u = (±sqrt(3))^3 - 3(±sqrt(3)) = ±3*sqrt(3) ∓ 3*sqrt(3) = 0.

✅ Why valid: Evaluating the cubic polynomial u*(u^2 - 3) at its root u^2 = 3 vanishes identically.

STEP-03 WARRANT

Calculate x + 1/x and x - 1/x given the square sum x^2 + 1/x^2 = K.

(x + 1/x)^2 = K + 2 => x + 1/x = sqrt(K + 2). (x - 1/x)^2 = K - 2 => x - 1/x = sqrt(K - 2).

✅ Why valid: Adding and subtracting the invariant 2 completes the square on the left-hand side.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Evaluate polynomials at x = 1/(sqrt(a) - b) by forming the minimal equation (x - b)^2 = a.

Rationalize: x = (sqrt(a) + b)/(a - b^2). When a - b^2 = 1, x - b = sqrt(a) => x^2 - 2bx + b^2 - a = 0. Divide P(x) by this quadratic.

✅ Why valid: The quadratic relation eliminates high degrees of x, reducing P(x) to its constant remainder.

x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}-b} = \sqrt{a}+b
Conjugate multiplication rationalizing unit reciprocal surds into standard quadratic roots.
x^3 + 1/x^3 = 0 \iff (x + 1/x)^2 = 3
The exact vanishing singularity where the cubic sum cancels identically to zero.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

CUBIC_SUM_FORMULA_AMNESIA Fallacy: Assuming x^3 + 1/x^3 = (x + 1/x)^3 without subtracting the cross-term 3(x + 1/x).

Diagnostic Context: When expanding (a + b)^3, does it equal just a^3 + b^3, or is there an intermediate cross-term?

Refutation & Repair Rule: (a + b)^3 = a^3 + b^3 + 3ab(a + b). Since ab = 1, you must subtract 3(x + 1/x) from (x + 1/x)^3.
OMITTING_SQUARE_ROOT_IN_RECOVERY Fallacy: Confusing (x + 1/x)^2 with x + 1/x, reporting K + 2 instead of sqrt(K + 2).

Diagnostic Context: If (x + 1/x)^2 = 29, what is the value of x + 1/x?

Refutation & Repair Rule: You must take the square root of both sides: x + 1/x = sqrt(29), not 29.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

Given that x^2 + 1/x^2 = 14: (i) Find the values of x + 1/x and x - 1/x (for x > 1). (ii) Find the value of x^3 + 1/x^3.

(i) (x + 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 + 2 = 14 + 2 = 16 => x + 1/x = sqrt(16) = 4.
(x - 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 - 2 = 14 - 2 = 12 => x - 1/x = sqrt(12) = 2*sqrt(3).
(ii) x^3 + 1/x^3 = (x + 1/x)^3 - 3(x + 1/x) = 4^3 - 3(4) = 64 - 12 = 52.

Core 1B · Dual-Stage Recall & 4-Stage Self-Tutor Flow

Before calculating numbers: If (x + 1/x)^2 = 3, what must be the value of x^3 + 1/x^3?

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Directly confronts the subtle cancellation identity: (x + 1/x)^3 - 3(x + 1/x) = 3*sqrt(3) - 3*sqrt(3) = 0.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

Given x^2 + 1/x^2 = 27: (1) Find the exact value of x + 1/x, (2) Find the exact value of x - 1/x, and (3) Determine if x + 1/x could ever equal 25.

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: (x + 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 + 2 = 27 + 2 = 29 => x + 1/x = sqrt(29) ≈ 5.385.
step_2: (x - 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 - 2 = 27 - 2 = 25 => x - 1/x = sqrt(25) = 5.
step_3: Compare values: x + 1/x = sqrt(29) != 25, and x - 1/x = 5 != 10.
conclusion: The claim that x + 1/x = 25 and x - 1/x = 10 is completely FALSE because it confuses the squared quantities with their square roots.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION FACTORIZATION_CUBIC_RECONSTRUCTION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: How can you factorize the sum of cubes a^3 + b^3 using the product of a linear and a quadratic factor?

Key Invariant Insight: a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2). For a = x and b = 1/x, this becomes (x + 1/x)(x^2 - 1 + 1/x^2).

💬 Inquiry: If (x + 1/x)^2 = 3, what is x^2 + 1/x^2?

Key Invariant Insight: x^2 + 1/x^2 = (x + 1/x)^2 - 2 = 3 - 2 = 1. Therefore, the factor (x^2 - 1 + 1/x^2) becomes (1 - 1) = 0! This proves x^3 + 1/x^3 = (x + 1/x)*(0) = 0 from a completely different factorization route!

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: If x = 1/(sqrt(5) - 2), what is the value of x^2 - 4x?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (A): Rationalizing yields x = sqrt(5) + 2 => x - 2 = sqrt(5) => (x - 2)^2 = 5 => x^2 - 4x + 4 = 5 => x^2 - 4x = 1.

RUNG 1 · CONCEPTUAL NUDGE

RUNG 2 · TACTICAL STEP

For rationalizing 1/(sqrt(5) - 2), multiply top and bottom by (sqrt(5) + 2). Note that 5 - 4 = 1, so x = sqrt(5) + 2.

Mathematical Domain: Polynomial Algebra over R, Factor Theorem, and Remainder Synthesis
🔗 Anchored to 1 Authenticated Core 2 Questions (Click to expand list)
SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2024-25-B-Q049
BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Definitions of polynomial degree, leading coefficient, and constant term.
  • Factor Theorem: (x - r) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(r) = 0.
  • Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c).
Hypotheses:
  • Let P(x) = x^3 - a*x^2 + b*x - c be a monic cubic polynomial with integer coefficients.
  • By the Rational Root Theorem, any integer root r must be an exact divisor of the constant term c.
  • If P(r) = 0, then (x - r) is a factor of P(x), and P(x) = (x - r) * Q(x) where deg(Q) = 2.
  • The remainder upon dividing P(x) by (x - k) equals P(k) by the Remainder Theorem.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Assuming non-divisor values of the constant term could be integer roots.
  • Confusing the remainder P(k) with P(-k) when dividing by (x - k).
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why systematic identification of an integral root via divisors of the constant term reduces a cubic polynomial of degree 3 to a quadratic quotient, enabling complete factorization into linear factors and rapid remainder evaluation without long polynomial division.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Identify all integer divisors of the constant term c of the monic cubic P(x) = x^3 - s1*x^2 + s2*x - s3.

If r is an integer root, r*(r^2 - s1*r + s2) = s3, so r must divide s3.

✅ Why valid: The Rational Root Theorem guarantees that rational roots of monic integer polynomials are integers dividing the constant term.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Test divisor candidates r in P(x) until finding a root where P(r) = 0.

Evaluate P(1), P(-1), P(2), etc. When P(r) = 0, conclude (x - r) is an exact factor.

✅ Why valid: Direct consequence of Euclid's Division Lemma for polynomials: P(x) = (x - r)Q(x) + P(r).

STEP-03 WARRANT

Divide P(x) by (x - r) to obtain the quadratic quotient Q(x), and factor Q(x) by splitting the middle term.

P(x)/(x - r) = x^2 + px + q = (x - beta)(x - gamma). Thus P(x) = (x - r)(x - beta)(x - gamma).

✅ Why valid: Every cubic polynomial over the reals decomposes into one linear factor and one quadratic factor.

STEP-04 WARRANT

To evaluate the remainder when P(x) is divided by (x - k), substitute x = k directly into either the expanded or factored form.

Remainder R = P(k) = (k - alpha)(k - beta)(k - gamma).

✅ Why valid: By the Remainder Theorem, P(k) = (k - k)Q(k) + R = 0 + R = R.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

SIGN_FLIP_IN_REMAINDER_THEOREM Fallacy: Evaluating P(-k) instead of P(k) when finding remainder modulo (x - k).

Diagnostic Context: When dividing by (x - 4), what value of x makes the divisor zero?

Refutation & Repair Rule: The divisor is (x - 4) = 0 => x = +4. Therefore, remainder is P(+4), NOT P(-4).
EXPANSION_ARITHMETIC_FATIGUE Fallacy: Performing long division to find remainders instead of evaluating the polynomial value directly.

Diagnostic Context: Is long division necessary to find the remainder upon linear division?

Refutation & Repair Rule: The Remainder Theorem guarantees R = P(c) in a single substitution step, eliminating 10+ lines of long division.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

Let P(x) = x^3 - 7x^2 + 14x - 8. (i) Factorise P(x) completely into linear factors. (ii) Find the remainder when P(x) is divided by (x - 5).

Divisors of 8 are ±1, ±2, ±4, ±8.
Test x = 1: P(1) = 1 - 7 + 14 - 8 = 0. Thus (x - 1) is a factor.
Divide P(x) by (x - 1): P(x) = (x - 1)(x^2 - 6x + 8).
Factor quadratic: x^2 - 6x + 8 = (x - 2)(x - 4).
Complete factorization: P(x) = (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 4).
(ii) By Remainder Theorem, remainder upon division by (x - 5) is P(5):
P(5) = (5 - 1)(5 - 2)(5 - 4) = (4)(3)(1) = 12.

Polynomials

Mathematical Domain: Radical Arithmetic, Minimal Polynomial Annihilators, and Nested Surds
🔗 Anchored to 1 Authenticated Core 2 Questions (Click to expand list)
SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-A-Q049
BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Rationalization of monomial and binomial surds using conjugate multipliers.
  • Construction of quadratic algebraic equations from radical roots.
  • Euclidean polynomial division: P(x) = Q(x)*D(x) + R(x) where deg(R) < deg(D).
Hypotheses:
  • Let 1/x = p - sqrt(q) with p^2 - q = 1, so that x = p + sqrt(q).
  • Isolating the radical: (x - p) = sqrt(q) => (x - p)^2 = q => x^2 - 2px + (p^2 - q) = 0.
  • The quadratic M(x) = x^2 - 2px + 1 vanishes identically at x = p + sqrt(q).
  • For any polynomial P(x), P(x) = Q(x)*M(x) + R(x) implies P(x) = 0 + R(x) = R(x).
  • For nested surds a = sqrt(u - sqrt(v)) and b = sqrt(u + sqrt(v)): (a + b)^2 = 2u + 2*sqrt(u^2 - v).
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Substituting x = p + sqrt(q) without rationalizing the denominator first.
  • Asserting that the square root of every positive real number is irrational (e.g. sqrt(4) = 2 in Q).
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why directly substituting a radical surd like x = p + sqrt(q) into a cubic or higher-order polynomial is computationally intractable, whereas isolating the radical to form the quadratic annihilator x^2 - 2px + (p^2 - q) = 0 reduces the entire polynomial to its linear remainder in one division step.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Rationalize the reciprocal surd 1/x = p - sqrt(q) by multiplying numerator and denominator by its conjugate p + sqrt(q).

x = (p + sqrt(q)) / ((p - sqrt(q))(p + sqrt(q))) = (p + sqrt(q)) / (p^2 - q).

✅ Why valid: Multiplying by conjugate rationalizes the denominator via difference of squares (a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Isolate the radical and square both sides to generate the monic quadratic annihilator M(x) = 0.

x - p = sqrt(q) => (x - p)^2 = q => x^2 - 2px + p^2 = q => x^2 - 2px + (p^2 - q) = 0.

✅ Why valid: Squaring both sides eliminates the radical while preserving algebraic equality on the branch x >= p.

STEP-03 WARRANT

Perform polynomial division of the target cubic P(x) by M(x) to express P(x) = Q(x)*M(x) + R(x).

Since M(x) = 0 at the evaluated surd, P(x) = Q(x)*(0) + R(x) = R(x).

✅ Why valid: Euclid's polynomial division lemma warrants uniqueness and degree reduction deg(R) < deg(M) = 2.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Evaluate nested radical sums (a + b) by squaring: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab.

When a = sqrt(u - sqrt(v)) and b = sqrt(u + sqrt(v)), a^2 + b^2 = 2u and 2ab = 2*sqrt(u^2 - v). Then a + b = sqrt(2u + 2*sqrt(u^2 - v)).

✅ Why valid: Identity (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 holds for all non-negative real numbers.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

BRUTE_FORCE_SURD_EXPANSION Fallacy: Expanding (2 + sqrt(3))^3 directly by binomial theorem instead of constructing the quadratic annihilator.

Diagnostic Context: If x satisfies x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0, can you replace higher powers of x without computing cube powers of irrational numbers?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Dividing by the annihilator polynomial reduces the cubic to a constant in 2 lines, eliminating error-prone binomial radical algebra.
UNIVERSAL_IRRATIONALITY_ASSUMPTION Fallacy: Believing that sqrt(n) is always irrational for every positive integer n.

Diagnostic Context: Is sqrt(4) = 2 or sqrt(9) = 3 irrational?

Refutation & Repair Rule: The square root of a perfect square is an integer (rational). Only non-square positive integers have irrational square roots.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

If 1/x = 3 - 2*sqrt(2): (i) Construct the quadratic polynomial equation satisfied by x. (ii) Evaluate x^3 - 5x^2 - 5x + 9 without direct radical expansion.

Step 1: Rationalize x: x = 1/(3 - 2*sqrt(2)) = (3 + 2*sqrt(2))/(9 - 8) = 3 + 2*sqrt(2).
Step 2: Form quadratic equation: x - 3 = 2*sqrt(2) => (x - 3)^2 = 8 => x^2 - 6x + 9 = 8 => x^2 - 6x + 1 = 0.
Step 3: Divide P(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 - 5x + 9 by (x^2 - 6x + 1):
x^3 - 5x^2 - 5x + 9 = (x + 1)(x^2 - 6x + 1) + 8.
Since x^2 - 6x + 1 = 0, P(x) = (x + 1)(0) + 8 = 8.

Core 1B · Dual-Stage Recall & 4-Stage Self-Tutor Flow

Complete the four unassisted retrieval gates to lock in procedural and conceptual mastery without teacher deferral.

STAGE 1 · PREDICT GATE UNASSISTED RECALL

Before performing long algebraic division: If x = 2 + sqrt(3), which monic quadratic equation does x satisfy identically?

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Forces isolation of radical (x - 2) = sqrt(3) and squaring to obtain x^2 - 4x + 4 = 3 => x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

Given 1/x = 2 - sqrt(3): (1) Rationalize 1/x to find x, (2) Deduce the quadratic relation satisfied by x, and (3) Evaluate the polynomial x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 5 using polynomial division by the quadratic relation.

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: x = 1/(2 - sqrt(3)) = (2 + sqrt(3))/(4 - 3) = 2 + sqrt(3).
step_2: x - 2 = sqrt(3) => (x - 2)^2 = 3 => x^2 - 4x + 4 = 3 => x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0.
step_3: Divide x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 5 by x^2 - 4x + 1: x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 5 = (x + 2)(x^2 - 4x + 1) + 3.
conclusion: Since x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0, the value is (x + 2)(0) + 3 = 3.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION DEGREE_REDUCTION_SUBSTITUTION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Instead of full polynomial long division, how can you express x^2 in terms of lower powers using x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0?

Key Invariant Insight: x^2 = 4x - 1! Multiplying by x gives x^3 = 4x^2 - x = 4(4x - 1) - x = 15x - 4.

💬 Inquiry: If you substitute x^3 = 15x - 4 and x^2 = 4x - 1 into x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 5, what happens to all the x terms?

Key Invariant Insight: (15x - 4) - 2(4x - 1) - 7x + 5 = (15 - 8 - 7)x + (-4 + 2 + 5) = 0x + 3 = 3! The variable cancels completely, leaving the exact integer constant!

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: Is the statement 'The square root of a positive real number is always an irrational number' True or False?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (B): A single counterexample disproves a universal claim: sqrt(4) = 2 is a rational number (in Q), refuting the assertion that all square roots of positive real numbers are irrational.

💡 2-Rung Scaffold Ladder (Non-Leaking Cognitive Anchors)

RUNG 1 · CONCEPTUAL NUDGE

Whenever you encounter high powers of a surd x = a + sqrt(b), isolate the radical (x - a) = sqrt(b) and square both sides to get an equation equal to zero.

RUNG 2 · TACTICAL STEP

Once you have x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0, divide the cubic polynomial by (x^2 - 4x + 1). The remainder is your answer because the quotient is multiplied by zero.

CODE: QUADS-PARALLELOGRAM-PROPERTIES

Quadrilaterals

Mathematical Domain: Euclidean Synthetic Geometry of Parallelograms and Triangle Midpoints
🔗 Anchored to 1 Authenticated Core 2 Questions (Click to expand list)
SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q046
BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Axiomatic properties of parallelograms: opposite sides are parallel and equal in length.
  • Sufficient condition for a quadrilateral to be a parallelogram: one pair of opposite sides is both parallel and equal.
  • Mid-Point Theorem and its Converse in Euclidean triangles.
Hypotheses:
  • Let ABCD be a parallelogram with AB = CD, AB || CD, and AD = BC, AD || BC.
  • If L in AB and M in CD satisfy AL = CM, then BL = AB - AL = CD - CM = DM.
  • Since BL || DM and BL = DM, quadrilateral BLDM is a parallelogram.
  • Diagonals of any parallelogram bisect each other => LM and BD bisect each other.
  • In triangle ABR, if P is midpoint of AB and PD || BR, then by converse of Mid-Point Theorem, D is midpoint of AR => AR = 2*AD = 2*BC.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Assuming a quadrilateral is a parallelogram without verifying that opposite sides are both parallel AND equal.
  • Asserting AR = BC when AR is double AD (and AD = BC).
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why establishing that a sub-quadrilateral has one pair of equal and parallel sides proves its diagonals bisect each other, and how the converse of the Mid-Point Theorem proves that parallel lines from midpoints double the exterior segment length rather than matching it.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Prove that quadrilateral BLDM inside parallelogram ABCD is itself a parallelogram.

Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB || CD => BL || DM. Since AB = CD and AL = CM, subtracting equals gives BL = AB - AL = CD - CM = DM.

✅ Why valid: A quadrilateral having one pair of opposite sides both equal and parallel is a parallelogram (Euclid Elements I.33).

STEP-02 WARRANT

Conclude that segment LM and diagonal BD bisect each other.

LM and BD are the diagonals of parallelogram BLDM.

✅ Why valid: The diagonals of any parallelogram bisect each other (Euclid Elements I.34).

STEP-03 WARRANT

Apply the converse of the Mid-Point Theorem to triangle ABR with PD || BR.

P is the midpoint of AB and line PD is drawn parallel to base BR, intersecting side AR at D. By the converse of the Mid-Point Theorem, D must be the midpoint of AR.

✅ Why valid: The line drawn through the midpoint of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Deduce the true scalar relationship between AR and BC.

Because D is the midpoint of AR, AR = 2*AD. In parallelogram ABCD, AD = BC. Therefore, AR = 2*BC.

✅ Why valid: Transitivity of equality and side lengths of a parallelogram.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

SUPERFICIAL_EQUALITY_ASSUMPTION Fallacy: Assuming AR = BC because D lies on AD and looks equal to BC without applying the Mid-Point Theorem.

Diagnostic Context: If D is the midpoint of AR, what is the relation between AR and AD?

Refutation & Repair Rule: D being the midpoint means AR = 2*AD. Since AD = BC, AR must equal 2*BC, which is twice the length, never equal!
MISSING_PARALLELOGRAM_CRITERION Fallacy: Thinking one must prove BOTH pairs of opposite sides are parallel before concluding a figure is a parallelogram.

Diagnostic Context: If one pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel, is that sufficient to declare a parallelogram?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Yes! One pair of opposite sides being both equal AND parallel is a fully sufficient condition to establish a parallelogram.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

In a parallelogram PQRS, points X and Y are taken on sides PQ and RS respectively such that PX = RY. Prove that: (i) XSYR is a parallelogram, and (ii) XY and SQ bisect each other.

In parallelogram PQRS, PQ = RS and PQ || RS.
Given PX = RY. Then QX = PQ - PX = RS - RY = SY.
Also, since PQ || RS, we have QX || SY.
Quadrilateral XQYS has one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel (QX = SY and QX || SY).
Therefore, XQYS is a parallelogram.
Since the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, the diagonals XY and QS bisect each other.

STAGE 1 · PREDICT GATE UNASSISTED RECALL

Before analyzing the full geometric diagram: In parallelogram ABCD, points L and M lie on opposite sides AB and CD such that AL = CM. What type of quadrilateral is formed by the remaining vertices BLDM?

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Guides the student to subtract equal segments AL = CM from equal sides AB = CD to recognize BL = DM and BL || DM.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

In triangle ABR, P is the mid-point of AB and a line through P parallel to BR meets AR at D. Given ABCD is a parallelogram, deduce the exact relation between AR and BC. Is AR = BC?

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: In triangle ABR, P is the midpoint of AB and PD || BR.
step_2: By the converse of the Mid-Point Theorem, D must be the midpoint of side AR.
step_3: Hence AR = 2 * AD.
conclusion: In parallelogram ABCD, opposite sides are equal: AD = BC. Substituting gives AR = 2 * BC. Therefore, AR is twice BC, so AR = BC is strictly FALSE.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION COORDINATE_GEOMETRY_VERIFICATION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Set up a coordinate frame: let A = (0,0), B = (2,0), D = (0,2), so C = (2,2). What are the coordinates of P (midpoint of AB)?

Key Invariant Insight: P is the midpoint of (0,0) and (2,0), so P = (1,0).

💬 Inquiry: If a line parallel to line PD passes through B(2,0) and meets line AD (y-axis) at R, what are the coordinates of R and the length of AR?

Key Invariant Insight: Slope of PD connecting (1,0) to (0,2) is -2. Line through B is y - 0 = -2(x - 2) => y = -2x + 4. At x = 0 (y-axis), y = 4 => R = (0,4). Thus AR = 4, while BC = AD = 2. This proves AR = 2*BC = 4, verifying AR = BC is definitively false!

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: If quadrilateral PQRS has PQ || RS and PQ = RS, what can be definitively concluded about its diagonals PR and QS?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (B): Because PQ || RS and PQ = RS, PQRS is a parallelogram. By the fundamental diagonal property of all parallelograms, its diagonals bisect each other.

Introduction to Euclid's Geometry

Mathematical Domain: Euclidean Axiomatic System & Synthetic Metric Geometry
🔗 Anchored to 2 Authenticated Core 2 Questions (Click to expand list)
SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2024-25-B-Q031SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q031
BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Understanding of points, straight line segments, and collinear point ordering.
  • Familiarity with Euclid's Common Notions regarding equality and whole-part relations.
Hypotheses:
  • Points P, Q, R, S lie in strict collinear order on straight line L.
  • The compound line segments satisfy length equality: PR = QS.
  • The intermediate segment QR is strictly positive and internal: P * Q * R and Q * R * S.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Non-collinear points in the plane.
  • Degenerate zero-length segments where P = Q or R = S.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why segment equality between overlapping collinear segments PR and QS guarantees equality of the non-overlapping end segments PQ and RS by direct retrieval and application of Euclid's Third Common Notion: 'If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal'.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Compound segment lengths can be partitioned into consecutive sub-segments: PR = PQ + QR and QS = QR + RS.

Because points P, Q, R, S are collinear in that sequence, point Q divides PR and point R divides QS. By Euclid's axiom of betweenness and segment addition, the whole equals the sum of its non-overlapping parts.

✅ Why valid: Euclid's Common Notion 5 ('The whole is greater than the part') establishes that collinear partitions sum strictly to the full length.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Given PR = QS, we state an initial equality between two whole magnitudes.

This is the premise explicitly provided in the hypothesis of the problem: PR = QS.

✅ Why valid: A premise is an assumed antecedent equality in deductive logic.

STEP-03 WARRANT

Subtracting the identical segment QR from both sides preserves equality: PR - QR = QS - QR.

Segment QR is identical to itself (Common Notion 4). When this common magnitude QR is removed from both equals (PR and QS), the remaining quantities must remain equal.

✅ Why valid: Euclid's Common Notion 3 explicitly warrants: 'If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal'.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Substituting the partitions yields the final theorem: PQ = RS.

Since PR - QR = PQ and QS - QR = RS, substituting these into PR - QR = QS - QR gives PQ = RS.

✅ Why valid: Substitution of equivalent expressions over a field or metric space preserves truth value.

Anchor: Invariant Vector Diagram

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

CONFUSING_AXIOM_WITH_POSTULATE Fallacy: Treating Common Notion 3 as a geometric postulate rather than a general axiom.

Diagnostic Context: What is the foundational difference between an Axiom (Common Notion) and a Postulate in Euclid's Elements?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Postulates are foundational assumptions specific to geometry (e.g., drawing a straight line, parallel lines). Common Notions (Axioms) are universal algebraic truths applicable to all mathematical magnitudes (numbers, lines, angles, areas).
COMMUTATIVITY_SUBTRACTION_FALLACY Fallacy: Assuming subtraction is commutative and writing QR - PR = QR - QS.

Diagnostic Context: Does the order of subtraction matter for directed geometric segments?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Subtraction of geometric magnitudes is non-commutative. Always subtract the smaller part from the whole (Whole - Part = Remainder).

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

Points P, Q, R, S are collinear in order. Prove that if PR = QS, then PQ = RS, citing Euclid's exact common notions.

Given PR = QS. Since Q lies between P and R, PR = PQ + QR. Since R lies between Q and S, QS = QR + RS. By Euclid's Common Notion 3 ('If equals are subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal'), we subtract QR from both sides: PR - QR = QS - QR. Since PR - QR = PQ and QS - QR = RS, it follows that PQ = RS. Q.E.D.

B is at -b, D is at +b (BC=CD=b). A is at -a, E is at +a (AC=CE=a). Length AB = |-b - (-a)| = a - b. Length DE = |a - b| = a - b. Since lengths are equal for all 0 < b < a, the proof is verified.'}

Core 1B · Dual-Stage Recall & 4-Stage Self-Tutor Flow

Complete the four unassisted retrieval gates to lock in procedural and conceptual mastery without teacher deferral.

STAGE 1 · PREDICT GATE UNASSISTED RECALL

Before calculating or substituting segments: You are given collinear points P, Q, R, S such that PR = QS. Which of Euclid's foundational Common Notions is the exact warrant for concluding that PQ = RS?

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Requires the student to retrieve and distinguish Euclid's Common Notions by operational role (subtraction vs addition vs transitivity) rather than guessing a geometric theorem.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

Formulate the exact algebraic step showing how subtracting segment QR from compound segments PR and QS formally establishes PQ = RS, explicitly naming the common notion applied.

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: Express PR and QS in terms of their non-overlapping partitions: PR = PQ + QR and QS = QR + RS.
step_2: Equate the two given equal quantities: PQ + QR = QR + RS.
step_3: Subtract the common segment QR from both sides: (PQ + QR) - QR = (QR + RS) - QR.
conclusion: By Euclid's Common Notion 3 ('If equals are subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal'), PQ = RS.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION REVERSE_ADDITION_RECONSTRUCTION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Suppose you are given the reverse problem: you know PQ = RS. Which Euclid Common Notion allows you to prove that PR = QS?

Key Invariant Insight: Common Notion 2 ('If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal'). Adding the identical shared segment QR to both equals produces PQ + QR = RS + QR, which gives PR = QS.

💬 Inquiry: What does this bidirectional symmetry teach you about Euclid's axiomatic structure?

Key Invariant Insight: Common Notion 2 (Addition) and Common Notion 3 (Subtraction) are exact dual operations that preserve equality across all metric decompositions.

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: Suppose point Q is moved continuously along the line until it coincides identically with point R (i.e., the length of shared segment QR collapses to 0). What happens to segments PR, QS, PQ, and RS, and does Euclid's relation still hold?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (B): At the boundary limit where length(QR) -> 0, points Q and R merge. Segment PQ becomes PR, and segment RS becomes QS. The subtraction of equals reduces to subtracting 0: PR - 0 = QS - 0 => PR = QS. The continuous perturbation preserves equality throughout the entire parameter domain.

RUNG 2 · TACTICAL STEP

BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Understanding of Cartesian coordinates (x, y) and standard linear equations in one variable.
  • Basic mastery of algebraic balance operations (adding/subtracting equals, scalar multiplication).
Hypotheses:
  • Let x and y denote distinct unknown real quantities (e.g. costs, rates, ages, coordinates).
  • Each independent condition in the problem stem defines a linear affine hyperplane: a*x + b*y = c.
  • The system is non-degenerate: det([a1, b1; a2, b2]) != 0, ensuring a unique model solution.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Degenerate parallel constraints that share no solution.
  • Assigning variable names without explicit units of measure.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why translating word problem constraints into linear algebraic equations requires identifying independent invariant quantities, assigning dimensional variables, formulating simultaneous linear constraints ax + by = c, and proving that the algebraic intersection represents the unique physical state satisfying all conditions.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Identify the two unknown target quantities and define them with precise units: let x be the first quantity and y be the second quantity.

A physical situation with two degrees of freedom requires two orthogonal coordinates to parameterize its state space.

✅ Why valid: Formal variable assignment establishes a bijective map between the physical word statement and the mathematical model.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Translate the first physical relationship into an exact linear equation: a1*x + b1*y = c1.

Summing the weighted contributions of each component equals the total measured value.

✅ Why valid: The principle of linear superposition warrants that composite totals equal the sum of their constituent parts.

STEP-03 WARRANT

Translate the second physical relationship into an independent linear equation: a2*x + b2*y = c2.

The second condition provides an independent constraint on the same variables (x, y).

✅ Why valid: Two non-parallel lines in the Cartesian plane R^2 intersect at exactly one point.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Solve the simultaneous system using elimination or substitution to extract the physical parameters.

Multiply equations by suitable scalar coefficients to eliminate one variable, solve for the remaining unknown, and back-substitute.

✅ Why valid: Elementary row operations preserve the exact solution set of a linear system.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

VARIABLE_UNIT_OMISSION Fallacy: Treating variables as dimensionless numbers and adding apples to rupees or hours to minutes.

Diagnostic Context: What are the physical dimensions of x and y, and do both sides of your equation have the same units?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Every term in an equation must possess identical physical dimensions (Dimensional Homogeneity Principle).
TRIAL_AND_ERROR_SUBSTITUTION_FALLACY Fallacy: Guessing numbers from the multiple-choice options without formulating the governing constraint equations.

Diagnostic Context: If the options were not provided, how would you systematically deduce the solution?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Competitive olympiad problems deliberately engineer options that trap guessers. Always formulate the two governing linear constraints first.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

The cost of 5 pens and 3 notebooks is Rs 105, while 3 pens and 4 notebooks cost Rs 85. Formulate the system of linear equations and find the cost of each item.

Let the cost of one pen be Rs x, and one notebook be Rs y. Condition 1 gives: 5x + 3y = 105. Condition 2 gives: 3x + 4y = 85. Multiplying the first equation by 4 gives: 20x + 12y = 420. Multiplying the second equation by 3 gives: 9x + 12y = 255. Subtracting eliminates y: 11x = 165 => x = 15. Substituting x = 15 into 3(15) + 4y = 85 gives 45 + 4y = 85 => 4y = 40 => y = 10. The cost of one pen is Rs 15 and one notebook is Rs 10.

Core 1B · Dual-Stage Recall & 4-Stage Self-Tutor Flow

Complete the four unassisted retrieval gates to lock in procedural and conceptual mastery without teacher deferral.

STAGE 1 · PREDICT GATE UNASSISTED RECALL

Before computing any algebraic values: A taxi service charges a fixed flag-fall rate plus a constant rate per kilometer. For a journey of 10 km, the total charge is Rs 105; for 15 km, the charge is Rs 155. If x represents the fixed charge in Rs, and y represents the rate per km in Rs/km, which mathematical model correctly represents this real-world system?

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Requires the student to correctly assign fixed overhead vs variable per-unit rate to their respective coefficients before attempting numerical evaluation.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

Formulate the two linear constraint equations from the taxi problem, and use elimination to determine the exact values of the fixed charge x and the per-km rate y.

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: Model equation 1 for 10 km: x + 10y = 105.
step_2: Model equation 2 for 15 km: x + 15y = 155.
step_3: Subtract equation 1 from equation 2: (x + 15y) - (x + 10y) = 155 - 105 => 5y = 50 => y = 10 Rs/km.
conclusion: Substitute y = 10 into equation 1: x + 10(10) = 105 => x + 100 = 105 => x = 5 Rs. Fixed charge is Rs 5, rate is Rs 10/km.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION RATE_OF_CHANGE_SLOPE_RECONSTRUCTION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Suppose you look at the problem from the perspective of differential rate of change: as distance increases from 10 km to 15 km (+5 km), the total cost increases from Rs 105 to Rs 155 (+Rs 50). What does the quotient (Delta Cost) / (Delta Distance) represent?

Key Invariant Insight: The slope m of the linear cost function, which is exactly the per-km variable charge y = 50 / 5 = 10 Rs/km.

💬 Inquiry: Once the slope y = 10 is known, how does evaluating at distance 0 yield the fixed charge x?

Key Invariant Insight: At distance d = 0, Cost(0) = Cost(10) - 10 * y = 105 - 100 = Rs 5. The fixed charge is simply the y-intercept of the affine line!

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: Suppose the two measured journeys were identical in distance (e.g. both 10 km), but one cost Rs 105 and the other cost Rs 115. What happens to the linear system and its solution?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (B): If x + 10y = 105 and x + 10y = 115, the coefficient determinant is 0 and the lines are strictly parallel: 105 != 115. In real-world data modeling, conflicting measurements create inconsistent systems, emphasizing that a valid model requires non-singular, non-contradictory observations.

BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Understanding of polynomial degrees, algebraic terms, and polynomial arithmetic (addition, multiplication).
  • Familiarity with evaluating algebraic functions P(x) at specific real values x = c.
Hypotheses:
  • Let P(x) in R[x] be a polynomial of degree n >= 1.
  • The linear divisor is D(x) = x - a.
  • Euclidean Division Theorem guarantees unique polynomials Q(x) and constant R such that P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + R.
  • Factor Theorem: (x - a) divides P(x) if and only if P(a) = 0.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Zero divisor D(x) = 0.
  • Division by higher-degree divisors without linear degree reduction.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why polynomial division P(x) = (x-a)Q(x) + R reduces the remainder to a single evaluation R = P(a), and how enforcing P(a) = 0 provides the exact algebraic warrant for linear factor divisibility and coefficient determination without executing long division.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Write the Euclidean division decomposition: P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + R.

By polynomial division theorem in R[x], dividing a polynomial of degree n by a linear divisor of degree 1 leaves a remainder of degree strictly less than 1, which is a constant scalar R.

✅ Why valid: Euclidean division theorem in the polynomial ring R[x].

STEP-02 WARRANT

Substitute x = a to eliminate the quotient term: P(a) = (a - a)Q(a) + R = 0 + R = R.

Setting x equal to the zero of the linear divisor forces the product (x - a)Q(x) to evaluate to 0.

✅ Why valid: Ring multiplication by zero property: 0 * Q(a) = 0.

STEP-03 WARRANT

State the Factor Theorem criterion: (x - a) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(a) = 0.

A polynomial (x - a) is a factor of P(x) if and only if the remainder R is zero, which means P(a) = 0.

✅ Why valid: Definition of algebraic divisibility in integral domains.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Determine the unknown parameter k by solving the algebraic equation P(a) = 0.

Substitute x = a into the parametric expression of P(x), equate the resulting scalar to 0, and isolate k.

✅ Why valid: Equivalence-preserving algebraic operations over the field R.

📊 Topic Visual Representation & Invariant Diagram

SVG VECTOR RIGOR (≥ 14px FONT)

🌉 Representation Bridge (Symbolic & Visual Mapping)

Anchor: Invariant Vector Diagram
P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + R
The exact identity expressing dividend as divisor times quotient plus scalar remainder.
R = P(a)
Evaluating at the root of the divisor vanishes the quotient, isolating the remainder.
P(a) = 0 <=> (x - a) | P(x)
A zero remainder is both necessary and sufficient for exact linear divisibility.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

DIVISOR_ROOT_SIGN_ERROR Fallacy: Evaluating P(-a) when the linear divisor is (x - a), or evaluating P(a) when the divisor is (x + a).

Diagnostic Context: What is the root of the divisor equation x - a = 0?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Always set the divisor to zero: x - a = 0 => x = a. For (x + a), x + a = 0 => x = -a.
LONG_DIVISION_COMPUTATIONAL_WASTE Fallacy: Performing full multi-step polynomial long division by hand to find remainder or verify a factor.

Diagnostic Context: Is long division necessary to find the remainder of P(x) divided by a linear term?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Use the Remainder/Factor Theorem: evaluating P(a) directly gives the remainder in a single step with zero risk of division arithmetic drift.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

Find the value of k if (x - 1) is a factor of P(x) = 2x^2 + kx + sqrt(2).

By the Factor Theorem, (x - 1) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(1) = 0. Substituting x = 1: P(1) = 2(1)^2 + k(1) + sqrt(2) = 2 + k + sqrt(2). Setting P(1) = 0 gives: 2 + k + sqrt(2) = 0 => k = -(2 + sqrt(2)). Q.E.D.

🎯 Independent Exit Task (Technique T12)

Complete the four unassisted retrieval gates to lock in procedural and conceptual mastery without teacher deferral.

STAGE 1 · PREDICT GATE UNASSISTED RECALL

Before calculating any coefficients: To determine if (2x - 1) is a factor of polynomial P(x) = 4x^3 - 4x^2 + x - 1, at what exact numerical value must you evaluate P(x)?

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Forces the student to solve the linear divisor root 2x - 1 = 0 => x = 1/2, preventing the sign error of using -1/2.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

Using the Factor Theorem, find the exact value of parameter k such that (x - 1) is a factor of P(x) = kx^2 - 3x + k.

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: Set the root of divisor x - 1 = 0 => x = 1.
step_2: By the Factor Theorem, (x - 1) divides P(x) if and only if P(1) = 0.
step_3: Substitute x = 1: P(1) = k(1)^2 - 3(1) + k = k - 3 + k = 2k - 3.
conclusion: Set 2k - 3 = 0 => 2k = 3 => k = 3/2.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION COEFFICIENT_MATCHING_RECONSTRUCTION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Suppose you solve the same problem without the Factor Theorem, by directly factoring P(x) = (x - 1)(kx - b). What must b be?

Key Invariant Insight: Expanding (x - 1)(kx - b) = kx^2 - (k + b)x + b. Matching the constant term gives b = k.

💬 Inquiry: Now match the linear coefficient -(k + b) to the given linear coefficient -3.

Key Invariant Insight: -(k + k) = -3 => -2k = -3 => k = 3/2. Synthetic coefficient matching confirms the exact same result independently!

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (B): At boundary k = 0, the leading quadratic term vanishes, degenerating P(x) to linear -3x. Its only zero is x = 0, so x - 1 cannot divide it. This confirms that k = 3/2 is the unique non-trivial value sustaining the factor property.

RUNG 2 · TACTICAL STEP

Set x = 1 in P(x) = kx^2 - 3x + k. You get k - 3 + k = 0. Combine the k terms and solve for k.

BLUEPRINT BP-CORE1A-CONSTRUCTION

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Understanding of parallelogram definitions, opposite parallel sides, and adjacent supplementary angles.
  • Familiarity with angle bisectors and triangle interior angle sum (180 degrees).
Hypotheses:
  • ABCD is a parallelogram with AB || CD and AD || BC.
  • Rays AP, BP, CQ, DQ bisect interior angles A, B, C, D respectively.
  • The four angle bisectors intersect at four points forming an enclosed quadrilateral PQRS.
  • Parallelogram ABCD is non-degenerate (angles are strictly between 0 and 180 degrees).
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Degenerate collinear vertices with area zero.
  • Rhombus limit where angle bisectors pass through vertices.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why the consecutive interior angles of any parallelogram sum to 180 degrees, forcing their bisected halves to sum to exactly 90 degrees, and how triangle angle sum transfers this invariant to prove that all four interior angles of the enclosed quadrilateral are strictly 90 degrees, forming a rectangle.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Consecutive interior angles of parallelogram ABCD are supplementary: angle(A) + angle(D) = 180 deg and angle(A) + angle(B) = 180 deg.

Since AB || CD and AD acts as a transversal, consecutive interior angles lie on the same side of the transversal and sum to 180 degrees.

✅ Why valid: Euclid's Parallel Postulate directly warrants that consecutive interior angles across parallel lines sum to two right angles (180 deg).

STEP-02 WARRANT

In triangle formed by the bisectors of angle A and angle D (say triangle APD), the sum of base angles is 90 degrees.

Ray AP bisects angle A, so angle(PAD) = 1/2 angle(A). Ray DP bisects angle D, so angle(PDA) = 1/2 angle(D). Therefore, angle(PAD) + angle(PDA) = 1/2 (angle(A) + angle(D)) = 1/2 (180 deg) = 90 deg.

✅ Why valid: Dividing an algebraic equality by 2 preserves exact mathematical equivalence over R.

STEP-03 WARRANT

The angle formed at intersection point P is exactly 90 degrees.

In triangle APD, the sum of all three angles is 180 degrees: angle(APD) = 180 deg - (angle(PAD) + angle(PDA)) = 180 deg - 90 deg = 90 deg.

✅ Why valid: The angle sum property of any Euclidean triangle guarantees that the three interior angles sum to 180 degrees.

STEP-04 WARRANT

By symmetry, all four interior angles of the enclosed quadrilateral PQRS are right angles (90 degrees), proving PQRS is a rectangle.

Applying the identical reasoning to consecutive pairs (A, B), (B, C), and (C, D) proves that the intersection angles at Q, R, and S are also 90 degrees. Vertically opposite angles transfer these 90-degree angles to the interior of quadrilateral PQRS. A quadrilateral whose four angles are 90 degrees is a rectangle.

✅ Why valid: A quadrilateral possessing four right angles satisfies the definitive invariant of a Euclidean rectangle.

📊 Topic Visual Representation & Invariant Diagram

🌉 Representation Bridge (Symbolic & Visual Mapping)

Anchor: Invariant Vector Diagram

angle(PSR) = angle(ASB) = 90 deg

A quadrilateral with all four interior angles equal to 90 degrees is by definition a rectangle.

⚠️ Trap Clinic & Misconception Repair (Technique T06)

SQUARE_ASSUMPTION_FALLACY Fallacy: Assuming the enclosed quadrilateral must be a square because all four angles are 90 degrees and the original figure is symmetrical.

Diagnostic Context: Are the adjacent sides of the enclosed quadrilateral PQRS necessarily equal in length when the parent parallelogram is not a rhombus (AB != AD)?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Four 90-degree angles prove the figure is a RECTANGLE. Equal adjacent sides require AB = AD (a rhombus). In a general parallelogram with unequal adjacent sides, the enclosed rectangle is strictly non-square.
COUNTEREXAMPLE_DISPROOF_OMISSION Fallacy: Treating a claim as true because it holds for one sketch, rather than testing whether a counterexample exists.

Diagnostic Context: How do you disprove a universal claim in mathematics?

Refutation & Repair Rule: A universal claim for all cases is disproved by exhibiting exactly ONE valid counterexample where the hypothesis holds but the conclusion fails.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

Prove that the quadrilateral formed by the bisectors of the four interior angles of any parallelogram is a rectangle.

Let ABCD be a parallelogram. Since AD || BC, consecutive interior angles A and B satisfy angle(A) + angle(B) = 180 deg. The bisectors of angle A and B meet at point S. In triangle ASB, angle(SAB) + angle(SBA) = 1/2(angle(A) + angle(B)) = 90 deg. Hence angle(ASB) = 180 - 90 = 90 deg. Vertically opposite angle angle(PSR) = 90 deg. Repeating this for all four pairs of consecutive angles proves angle(P) = angle(Q) = angle(R) = angle(S) = 90 deg. Therefore, PQRS is a rectangle. Q.E.D.

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: In parallelogram ABCD with AD || BC, consecutive interior angles on the same side of transversal AB are supplementary: angle(A) + angle(B) = 180 deg.
step_2: Since ray AS bisects angle A and ray BS bisects angle B, angle(SAB) = (1/2) * angle(A) and angle(SBA) = (1/2) * angle(B).
step_3: Their sum in triangle ASB is angle(SAB) + angle(SBA) = (1/2) * (angle(A) + angle(B)) = (1/2) * 180 deg = 90 deg.
step_4: By the triangle angle sum theorem in triangle ASB, angle(ASB) = 180 deg - 90 deg = 90 deg.
conclusion: Since line segments AP and CR intersect at S, the interior angle of quadrilateral PQRS at vertex S is vertically opposite to angle(ASB), so angle(PSR) = angle(ASB) = 90 deg.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION COORDINATE_AND_SLOPE_ORTHOGONALITY_RECONSTRUCTION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Suppose instead of synthetic Euclidean angle-sum, we assign coordinates with vertex A at origin (0,0), side AB along positive x-axis of length a, and AD at angle theta. What are the direction angles of bisector AS and bisector BS?

Key Invariant Insight: Bisector AS makes angle theta/2 with the positive x-axis. Bisector BS bisects angle B = (180 - theta), so relative to ray BA (negative x-axis), it makes angle (180 - theta)/2 = 90 - theta/2.

💬 Inquiry: What is the angle between the two lines in the plane?

Key Invariant Insight: The angle between line AS (inclination theta/2) and line BS (inclination 180 - (90 - theta/2) = 90 + theta/2) is exactly (90 + theta/2) - (theta/2) = 90 degrees, proving perpendicularity regardless of theta or side lengths!

💬 Inquiry: How does this independent slope derivation reinforce the synthetic proof?

Key Invariant Insight: It demonstrates that the orthogonality is an algebraic invariant of the parallel lines condition, completely independent of the choice of diagram or scaling.

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: Suppose parallelogram ABCD is continuously deformed so that all four sides become equal (a rhombus), or deformed into a rectangle. What happens to the enclosed quadrilateral PQRS at these boundary limits?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (A): In a rhombus, diagonals bisect the opposite angles, meaning opposite angle bisectors coincide and all four bisectors intersect at the single central point of symmetry (collapsing PQRS to a point of area 0). In a rectangle where angles are already 90 degrees, each bisector is at 45 degrees, creating isosceles right triangles at each corner and forcing the enclosed rectangle to have equal adjacent sides, becoming a square.

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Familiarity with spatial cruciform/Cartesian axis orientations (Top-Bottom, Left-Right).
Hypotheses:
  • Each circular or cruciform figure specifies four peripheral integers: Top (T), Bottom (B), Left (L), Right (R), and one internal target value C.
  • Vertical axis difference: Delta_V = T - B.
  • Horizontal axis difference: Delta_H = R - L.
  • Central synthesis invariant: C = (Delta_V + Delta_H)^2.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Degenerate single-axis arithmetic that ignores one coordinate dimension.
  • Random non-invariant formulas that do not hold across all given exemplars.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why the central number cannot be derived from a single axis alone, but requires decomposing the 4-node peripheral system into two orthogonal directional differences (vertical difference and horizontal difference), synthesizing their linear sum, and composing with a non-linear squaring map to generate the invariant central value.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Calculate the vertical axis directional difference Delta_V = T - B for each figure.

In Figure 1: 12 - 4 = 8. In Figure 2: 15 - 6 = 9. In Figure 3: 9 - 5 = 4.

✅ Why valid: Standard integer subtraction along the vertical coordinate dimension.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Calculate the horizontal axis directional difference Delta_H = R - L for each figure.

In Figure 1: 10 - 7 = 3. In Figure 2: 9 - 9 = 0. In Figure 3: 14 - 6 = 8.

✅ Why valid: Standard integer subtraction along the orthogonal horizontal coordinate dimension.

STEP-03 WARRANT

Synthesize the two orthogonal differences into a composite base S = Delta_V + Delta_H.

In Figure 1: 8 + 3 = 11. In Figure 2: 9 + 0 = 9. In Figure 3: 4 + 8 = 12.

✅ Why valid: Linear addition combines independent directional variations into a single scalar invariant.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Square the synthesized scalar to determine the center: C = S^2.

In Figure 1: 11^2 = 121 (matches given center). In Figure 2: 9^2 = 81 (matches given center). In Figure 3: 12^2 = 144.

✅ Why valid: Applying the invariant quadratic transformation established across figures 1 and 2 to figure 3 guarantees uniqueness and consistency.

Refutation & Repair Rule: Cruciform puzzle architectures couple both orthogonal axes. Both vertical and horizontal numbers contribute to the central result.
DIRECTIONAL_SIGN_INCONSISTENCY Fallacy: Subtracting bottom minus top in one figure and top minus bottom in another figure.

Diagnostic Context: Must the direction of subtraction remain fixed across all figures?

Refutation & Repair Rule: The geometric orientation (Top - Bottom, Right - Left) must be strictly invariant across every exemplar in the series.

Core 1A · Constructive Universal Proof & Declarative Anchor

📐 Conventions and Scope & Entry Assumptions

  • Understanding of circular degrees, complete circle rotation (360 degrees), and proportional scaling.
  • Familiarity with reading data from frequency tables, bar charts, and pie charts.
Hypotheses:
  • In a circular pie chart, the complete circumference subtends exactly 360 degrees at the center.
  • The central angle theta_i of any category sector is strictly proportional to its frequency: theta_i = (Value_i / Total) * 360 deg.
  • In a dual-year bar graph, the vertical axis maps bar heights linearly to monetary expenditure.
Excluded / Boundary Values:
  • Distorted 3D perspectives that alter apparent sector angles.
  • Dividing central angles by 100 instead of 360 degrees.
⚡ The Inferential Leap (Technique T02):

Why reading and converting statistical visual representations (pie chart central angles and grouped bar heights) requires establishing the exact proportional metric scaling factor (Theta / 360 = Value / Total), mapping visual angular sectors to raw quantitative frequencies without distortion.

🪜 Completed Teaching Path (Step-by-Step Rigorous Derivation)

STEP-01 WARRANT

Calculate the unit degree value factor: for total marks T = 720, each degree represents 720 / 360 = 2 marks.

The complete circle is 360 degrees. By uniform metric distribution, dividing total magnitude by 360 yields the constant rate per degree.

✅ Why valid: Linear proportional scaling preserves relative frequency across circular partitions.

STEP-02 WARRANT

Determine the required total sector angle corresponding to 250 marks: theta_req = 250 / 2 = 125 degrees.

Since every degree equals 2 marks, dividing the target 250 marks by 2 marks/degree gives exactly 125 degrees.

✅ Why valid: Dimensional analysis: marks divided by (marks/degree) yields pure degrees.

STEP-03 WARRANT

Test pairwise sums of subject central angles to find which pair equals 125 degrees.

Inspect the pie chart sectors: Social Science = 65 deg, Mathematics = 90 deg, English = 55 deg, Hindi = 70 deg, Science = 80 deg. The sum English (55 deg) + Hindi (70 deg) = 125 deg.

✅ Why valid: Exact integer addition of angular sub-sectors: 55 + 70 = 125 degrees.

STEP-04 WARRANT

Verify marks: English (55 * 2 = 110) + Hindi (70 * 2 = 140) = 250 marks, confirming English and Hindi.

Multiplying the confirmed angular sectors by 2 marks/degree confirms 110 + 140 = 250 marks.

✅ Why valid: Direct arithmetic evaluation verifies that the visual representation maps bijectively to the target value.

PERCENTAGE_DEGREE_CONFUSION Fallacy: Treating sector degrees as percentages and calculating Value = (theta / 100) * Total.

Diagnostic Context: How many total degrees exist in a full circle, and why is dividing by 100 a catastrophic error?

Refutation & Repair Rule: A full circle has 360 degrees, not 100. Always divide by 360. If percentage is needed, multiply the fraction (theta / 360) by 100%.
VISUAL_AREA_ESTIMATION_FALLACY Fallacy: Guessing which sector is larger by eye rather than reading the explicit degree label.

Diagnostic Context: Can visual angles be distorted by perspective or diagram printing?

Refutation & Repair Rule: Always use the exact quantitative labels (degrees or frequencies) printed on the visual representation.

⚓ Worked Concept Anchor (Canonical Olympiad Exemplar)

A pie chart represents total marks of 720. Sectors are: Social Science 65 deg, Math 90 deg, English 55 deg, Hindi 70 deg, Science 80 deg. Which two subjects total 250 marks?

Each degree represents 720 / 360 = 2 marks. To obtain 250 marks, the combined central angle must be 250 / 2 = 125 deg. Summing angles: English (55 deg) + Hindi (70 deg) = 125 deg. English marks = 55 * 2 = 110; Hindi marks = 70 * 2 = 140; Total = 250 marks. Therefore, the subjects are English and Hindi.

The sector angle for Rent is 100 degrees, Food is 120 degrees, Education is 80 degrees, and the remainder is Savings. Find: (i) the sector angle for Savings, (ii) the exact amount spent on Education, and (iii) how much more money is spent on Food than on Rent.

Core 1B · Dual-Stage Recall & 4-Stage Self-Tutor Flow

Complete the four unassisted retrieval gates to lock in procedural and conceptual mastery without teacher deferral.

STAGE 1 · PREDICT GATE UNASSISTED RECALL

Before computing individual subject marks: If a circular pie chart represents an examination total of 720 marks across 360 degrees, how many marks does each 1 degree of central angle represent?

View Predict Rationale & Mechanism

Requires the student to calculate the fundamental visual-to-numerical conversion ratio (720 / 360 = 2) before attempting multi-subject calculations.

STAGE 2 · ACTIVE ATTEMPT LOCKED UNTIL COMMITMENT

Using the 2 marks/degree scaling factor, find which two subjects among Social Science (65 deg), Math (90 deg), English (55 deg), Hindi (70 deg), Science (80 deg) total exactly 250 marks.

Reveal Autonomous Model Proof (Post-Attempt)
step_1: Calculate the target combined angle: theta_target = 250 marks / (2 marks/deg) = 125 deg.
step_2: Test combinations of given sector angles: 55 deg (English) + 70 deg (Hindi) = 125 deg.
step_3: Confirm individual marks: English = 55 * 2 = 110 marks; Hindi = 70 * 2 = 140 marks.
conclusion: Total marks = 110 + 140 = 250 marks. The subjects are English and Hindi.
STAGE 3 · REVERSE RECONSTRUCTION FRACTIONAL_PERCENTAGE_RECONSTRUCTION

Reverse reconstruction stress-tests conceptual stability by solving via an alternative invariant route:

💬 Inquiry: Suppose instead of working in degrees, we compute the target fraction of the total exam: 250 / 720. What is this fraction in simplest form?

Key Invariant Insight: 250 / 720 = 25 / 72.

💬 Inquiry: What fraction of the circle's 360 degrees does 25 / 72 represent?

Key Invariant Insight: (25 / 72) * 360 = 25 * 5 = 125 degrees. The fractional route yields identical degree requirements without assuming unit scaling first!

STAGE 4 · BOUNDARY TEST & LIMITING CASE CHANGED GIVENS & PERTURBATION

Perturbation & Boundary Test: Suppose the examination scoring scale is uniformly doubled so that the total marks become 1440 instead of 720, but each student's relative score in every subject remains unchanged. What happens to the central angles of the pie chart sectors?

Check Boundary Test & Limiting Case Result

Correct Option (B): Sector central angle is defined by theta_i = (Value_i / Total) * 360 deg. When values and total are both scaled by factor k, the scaling factors cancel: (k * Value_i) / (k * Total) = Value_i / Total. Central angles are scale-invariant representations of relative proportions.

RUNG 2 · TACTICAL STEP

Since 1 deg = 2 marks, 250 marks requires an angle of 250 / 2 = 125 deg. Look for two subject angles that sum to 125.
